source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.8.ANFR.2: Covers all the summary's skills: a function as one output per input (pairs, tables, situations, rules), using rules, increasing/decreasing and where, linear vs non-linear (pairs, equations, descriptions), the shapes of graphs from real situations (described in words, since no figure may be shown), and patterns of change in non-linear functions.
notes.NC26.8.ANFR.3: Covers the summary: identifying linear functions and slope-intercept form, reading slope and intercept, writing equations, slope from points and tables, intercepts from a point, interpreting slope and intercept in situations, graphing described in words (points on a line, intercepts, steepness; no figures shown), comparing functions given as equations, tables, points and situations, and rewriting equations.
notes.NC26.8.ANFR.4: Written from the summary alone, for the adaptive check-up. Text only: placement on a number line is asked as "between which numbers" or "how many whole numbers lie between". Repeating decimals are only recognised as rational, not converted to fractions.
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.1: Transformations are tested with coordinates written as (x, y); no grid or drawing is referred to. Rotations are 90 degrees about the origin only.
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.2: Dilations are tested with coordinates and lengths; drawing a dilation is not tested.
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.3: All side lengths are given in the text. SSA cases (obtuse angle, and the one with the height given) are stated with the needed distance or hint so that no figure is needed. The three-angles-only cases rely on "triangles of the same size and shape count as one".
notes.NC26.8.RD.3: Written from the standard summary only. Every key was computed from the data by an independent statistics function and cross-checked against the compute string. Quartiles use the median-of-halves method, and each stem that needs it says so. Displays (dot plots, stem-and-leaf, box plots, histograms) are described in words or as lists and five-number summaries.
notes.NC26.8.RD.2: Statistical questions about 3-4 populations, bias, random sampling, simulation and organizing data; all answers computed or counted in the builder.
notes.NC26.8.RD.4: Standard deviation is the population form (the square root of the mean of the squared distances from the mean), defined in each computing question. Answers are built to be exact; two questions have decimal variances (13.2 and 5.4).
notes.NC26.8.RD.5: No figures: every data set is a list of values or given as summaries (means, medians, ranges, quartiles) in words. Ten skills of nine questions each (three at each difficulty). Quartiles use the median-of-halves method; for an odd number of values the stem says not to count the median in either half. The MAD question defines MAD in its stem. Sampling and methods (S9) are choice questions only.
notes.NC26.8.ANFR.5: Written from the summary alone, for the adaptive check-up. Radicals are covered as evaluating and solving with square and cube roots (including of fractions and negative cubes); no questions on simplifying a non-perfect-square radical, which the summary does not name. Scientific-notation answers that are not whole numbers are asked as choices.
notes.NC26.8.RD.1: All answers were computed; counts of outcomes were checked by enumeration in the builder.
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.4: No figures: every configuration is described by names (corresponding, alternate interior, same-side interior, exterior angle at a named vertex) or, in the "positions" skill, by above/below the upper or lower parallel line and left/right of the transversal. Triangle and parallel-line questions name the points and the line that is extended.
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.5: Text only: every distance, side and coordinate is written in the stem. Radical answers are choice questions; the few rounded numeric answers say how to round (keys checked away from a rounding boundary).
notes.NC26.8.SGMR.6: Text only: every dimension is written in the stem. Pyramids are mostly square-based, with rectangular and triangular bases too; surface area of cones and spheres is left out because the summary names only pyramids. Slant-height problems use the Pythagorean Theorem (grade 8). Answers with pi are choice questions or ask for the coefficient k.

questions.skill: Solve a linear equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $5x + 3 = 2x + 15$
questions.solution: Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $3x + 3 = 15$. Subtract 3 from both sides: $3x = 12$. Divide by 3: $x = 4$. Check: $5(4) + 3 = 23$ and $2(4) + 15 = 23$.

questions.skill: Write an equation from a situation with two quantities
questions.stem: Maya has 5 dollars and saves 2 dollars each week. Leo has 11 dollars and saves 1 dollar each week. Let $w$ be the number of weeks. Which equation says that they have the same amount of money after $w$ weeks?
questions.solution: After $w$ weeks Maya has $5 + 2w$ dollars (5 to start, 2 more each week). Leo has $11 + w$ dollars. "The same amount" means the two are equal: $5 + 2w = 11 + w$.

solve.work: Maya after w weeks: 5 + 2w. Leo: 11 + 1w = 11 + w. Same amount: 5 + 2w = 11 + w. Other options mix up the start and the rate.

questions.skill: Find the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What is the greatest whole number $x$ that makes $4x - 5 < x + 7$ true?
questions.solution: Subtract $x$ from both sides: $3x - 5 < 7$. Add 5: $3x < 12$. Divide by 3: $x < 4$. The greatest whole number less than 4 is 3. Check: for $x = 3$, $4(3) - 5 = 7$ and $3 + 7 = 10$, and $7 < 10$. For $x = 4$ both sides equal 11, so 4 does not work.

solve.work: 4x - 5 < x + 7 -> 3x < 12 -> x < 4. Greatest whole number below 4 is 3. Check x=3: 7 < 10 true; x=4: 11 < 11 false.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $8x - 6 = 5x + 9$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $3x = 15$. Divide both sides by $3$: $x = 5$. Check: with $x = 5$ both sides equal $34$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What value of $x$ makes this equation true? $13 + 2x = 5x - 8$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $2x + 13 = 5x - 8$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-3x = -21$. Divide both sides by $-3$: $x = 7$. Check: with $x = 7$ both sides equal $27$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Find the solution of $4x + 3 = 9x + 18$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-5x = 15$. Divide both sides by $-5$: $x = -3$. Check: with $x = -3$ both sides equal $-9$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ makes $2x + 9 = 5x$ true?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-3x = -9$. Divide both sides by $-3$: $x = 3$. Check: with $x = 3$ both sides equal $15$. The other choices come from moving terms the wrong way, for example adding $2x$ and $5x$ together.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $4x + 4 = 2x + 12$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x = 8$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x = 4$. Check: with $x = 4$ both sides equal $20$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: Find the value of $x$ that solves $3x = 2(x + 7)$.
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $3x = 2x + 14$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $x = 14$. Check: with $x = 14$ both sides equal $42$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: Which equation is the result of using the distributive property on the left side of $4(2x - 3) = x + 5$?
questions.solution: The 4 multiplies both terms inside the parentheses: $4(2x - 3) = 4 \cdot 2x - 4 \cdot 3 = 8x - 12$. So the equation becomes $8x - 12 = x + 5$. The other choices multiply only one of the terms, change a sign, or multiply the wrong term.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $6x - 2x + 7 = x + 19$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $4x + 7 = x + 19$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $3x = 12$. Divide both sides by $3$: $x = 4$. Check: with $x = 4$ both sides equal $23$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.stem: What is the left side of $7x + 3 - 2x - 8 = 4x + 1$ after combining like terms?
questions.solution: Combine the $x$ terms: $7x - 2x = 5x$. Combine the numbers: $3 - 8 = -5$. So the left side is $5x - 5$. The other choices add $7x$ and $2x$, get the sign of the numbers wrong, or add 3 and 8.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $0.5x + 4 = 0.3x + 6$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0.2x = 2$. Divide both sides by $0.2$: $x = 10$. Check: with $x = 10$ both sides equal $9$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: What value of $x$ solves $\frac{x}{2} + 3 = x - 1$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $\frac{1}{2}x + 3 = x - 1$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-\frac{1}{2}x = -4$. Divide both sides by $-\frac{1}{2}$: $x = 8$. Check: with $x = 8$ both sides equal $7$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: What is the smallest whole number you can multiply both sides of $\frac{x}{3} + 2 = \frac{x}{2}$ by to clear all of the fractions?
questions.solution: The denominators are 3 and 2. The smallest number that both 3 and 2 divide into is 6. Multiplying by 6 gives $2x + 12 = 3x$, with no fractions. Multiplying by 3 leaves $\frac{3x}{2}$, and 12 works but is not the smallest.

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: How many solutions does $2x + 5 = 2x + 9$ have?
questions.answer: No solution
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = 4$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is never true, so there is no solution.

solve.answer: No solution

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: Which statement about $6x - 4 = 6x - 4$ is true?
choices: It is true for exactly one value of $x$
It is true for every value of $x$
It is true for no value of $x$
It is true for exactly two values of $x$
questions.answer: It is true for every value of $x$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = 0$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is always true, so every number is a solution.

solve.answer: It is true for every value of $x$
solve.work: Both sides identical, so true for every x.

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: The equation $2x + 7 = 2x + k$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: For infinitely many solutions, both sides must be the same expression. The $x$ terms already match, so the numbers must match: $k = 7$.

solve.work: Same x-coefficient; infinitely many requires constants equal: k = 7.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: Three times a number, decreased by 4, equals the number increased by 10. Which equation represents this, where $n$ is the number?
questions.solution: "Three times a number" is $3n$, "decreased by 4" is $3n - 4$, and "the number increased by 10" is $n + 10$. Setting them equal gives $3n - 4 = n + 10$. The other choices put the 4 inside the multiplication, use plus instead of minus, or multiply the number by 10.

solve.work: Three times n, decreased by 4: 3n - 4. Number increased by 10: n + 10.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: One taxi charges 3 dollars plus 2 dollars per mile. Another taxi charges 1 dollar plus 3 dollars per mile. Let $m$ be the number of miles. Which equation says that the two charges are equal?
questions.solution: The first charge is 3 plus 2 for each mile: $3 + 2m$. The second is 1 plus 3 for each mile: $1 + 3m$. Equal charges give $3 + 2m = 1 + 3m$. The other choices swap the fixed fee and the rate, leave out the 1, or use the wrong rate.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: Five times a number plus 8 equals nine times the number minus 12. What is the number?
questions.solution: Let $n$ be the number: $5n + 8 = 9n - 12$. Subtract $5n$ from both sides: $8 = 4n - 12$. Add 12 to both sides: $20 = 4n$. Divide by 4: $n = 5$. Check: $5(5) + 8 = 33$ and $9(5) - 12 = 33$.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: A tank holds 50 liters and loses 4 liters every minute. A second tank holds 10 liters and gains 6 liters every minute. After how many minutes will the two tanks hold the same amount?
questions.solution: After $m$ minutes the first tank holds $50 - 4m$ liters and the second holds $10 + 6m$ liters. Set them equal: $50 - 4m = 10 + 6m$. Then $40 = 10m$, so $m = 4$. Check: $50 - 16 = 34$ and $10 + 24 = 34$.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which inequality shows all of the solutions of $5x + 2 > 2x + 11$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $3x > 9$. Divide both sides by $3$: $x > 3$. The other choices reverse the sign, forget to divide by 3, or add the $x$ terms instead of subtracting.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What is the least whole number $x$ that makes $6x - 3 > 2x + 9$ true?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $4x > 12$. Divide both sides by $4$: $x > 3$. Since $x$ must be greater than 3, the least whole number is 4. (Check: $6(4) - 3 = 21 > 2(4) + 9 = 17$.)

solve.work: 4x > 12 -> x > 3; least whole number 4 (x = 3 gives 15 > 15, false).

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ is a solution of $3x + 1 < x + 9$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x < 8$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x < 4$. Only 3 is less than 4. (At $x = 4$ both sides equal 13, so 4 is not a solution.)

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: Which inequality shows all of the solutions of $-2x > 8$?
questions.solution: Divide both sides by $-2$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality, so $>$ becomes $<$: $x < -4$. (Check: $x = -5$ gives $-2(-5) = 10 > 8$.)

solve.issues: Only one side has a variable; not an equation/inequality with the variable on both sides, though it tests the sign-reversal property used in this standard.

questions.skill: Write an inequality for a situation
questions.stem: Club A charges 10 dollars to join plus 3 dollars per visit. Club B charges 4 dollars to join plus 5 dollars per visit. Let $h$ be the number of visits. Which inequality says that Club A costs less than Club B?
questions.solution: Club A costs $10 + 3h$ and Club B costs $4 + 5h$. "Costs less than" means $<$, so the inequality is $10 + 3h < 4 + 5h$. The other choices use the wrong sign, swap the joining fees and the rates, or leave out the 4.

questions.skill: Write an inequality for a situation
questions.stem: Four times a number, plus 3, is at most twice the number minus 9. Which inequality represents this, where $n$ is the number?
questions.solution: "At most" means less than or equal to, so the symbol is $\le$. "Four times a number, plus 3" is $4n + 3$ and "twice the number minus 9" is $2n - 9$. The other choices use $\ge$ (at least), $<$ (which leaves out equal), or put the 3 inside the multiplication.

questions.skill: Name or count the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality
questions.stem: How many whole numbers $x$ (0, 1, 2, 3, ...) make $3x + 2 < x + 10$ true?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x < 8$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x < 4$. The whole numbers less than 4 are 0, 1, 2 and 3, which is 4 numbers.

questions.skill: Name or count the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality
questions.stem: What is the least integer that makes $6x + 1 \ge 2x + 21$ true?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $4x \ge 20$. Divide both sides by $4$: $x \ge 5$. So $x$ is 5 or greater, and the least integer is 5.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solving $3x + 5 = x + 13$ wrote $4x + 5 = 13$ as her first step. What is wrong with this step?
choices: Nothing is wrong with this step
She should have divided both sides by 3 first
She added $x$ on the left but subtracted $x$ on the right; $x$ should be subtracted from both sides
She should have subtracted 5 from the left side only
questions.answer: She added $x$ on the left but subtracted $x$ on the right; $x$ should be subtracted from both sides
questions.solution: To move $x$ off the right side, subtract $x$ from both sides: $3x - x + 5 = 13$, which is $2x + 5 = 13$. The student added $x$ on the left ($3x + x = 4x$) but subtracted $x$ on the right, so the two sides were not changed in the same way.

solve.answer: She added $x$ on the left but subtracted $x$ on the right; $x$ should be subtracted from both sides
solve.work: From 3x + 5 = x + 13, removing x from the right but adding to the left gives 4x; correct is subtract x from both: 2x + 5 = 13.

questions.skill: Check a solution and justify the steps
questions.stem: Is $x = 4$ a solution of $3x - 2 = 2x + 2$?
choices: No, because the left side is 10 and the right side is 12
No, because the left side is 14 and the right side is 10
questions.answer: Yes, because both sides equal 10
questions.solution: Substitute $x = 4$. Left side: $3(4) - 2 = 12 - 2 = 10$. Right side: $2(4) + 2 = 8 + 2 = 10$. The sides are equal, so $x = 4$ is a solution.

solve.answer: Yes, because both sides equal 10

questions.skill: Check a solution and justify the steps
questions.stem: When $x = 5$, both sides of $4x - 3 = 2x + 7$ have the same value. What is that value?
questions.solution: Left side: $4(5) - 3 = 20 - 3 = 17$. Right side: $2(5) + 7 = 10 + 7 = 17$. Each side equals 17.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $4(x - 2) = 2x + 6$
questions.solution: Distribute: $4x - 8 = 2x + 6$. Subtract $2x$: $2x - 8 = 6$. Add 8: $2x = 14$. Divide by 2: $x = 7$. Check: $4(7 - 2) = 20$ and $2(7) + 6 = 20$.

questions.skill: Recognise an equation with infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: How many solutions does the equation $3(x + 2) = 3x + 6$ have?
questions.answer: Infinitely many solutions
questions.solution: Distribute on the left: $3x + 6 = 3x + 6$. Both sides are exactly the same expression, so the equation is true for every value of $x$. It has infinitely many solutions.

solve.answer: Infinitely many solutions
solve.work: 3(x + 2) = 3x + 6, identical to the right side, so every x works: infinitely many solutions.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality where dividing by a negative reverses the sign
questions.stem: Which inequality shows all the solutions of $5 - 2x \ge x - 7$?
questions.answer: $x \le 4$
questions.solution: Add $2x$ to both sides: $5 \ge 3x - 7$. Add 7: $12 \ge 3x$. Divide by 3: $4 \ge x$, which is the same as $x \le 4$. Check: $x = 0$ gives $5 \ge -7$, which is true.

solve.answer: $x \le 4$

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-6x = -36$. Divide both sides by $-6$: $x = 6$. Check: with $x = 6$ both sides equal $-10$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which equation has the solution $x = 6$?
questions.solution: Put $x = 6$ into each equation. In $3x - 4 = x + 8$ the left side is $3(6) - 4 = 14$ and the right side is $6 + 8 = 14$, so it works. In $3x + 4 = x + 8$ the sides are 22 and 14. In $3x - 4 = x - 8$ they are 14 and $-2$. In $4x - 3 = 2x + 8$ they are 21 and 20.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $8x - 4 = 3x + 6$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $5x = 10$. Divide both sides by $5$: $x = 2$. Check: with $x = 2$ both sides equal $12$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: What value of $x$ makes this equation true? $-2(x - 5) = 3x + 15$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-2x + 10 = 3x + 15$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-5x = 5$. Divide both sides by $-5$: $x = -1$. Check: with $x = -1$ both sides equal $12$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ is the solution of $2(3x + 1) = 4(x + 4)$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $6x + 2 = 4x + 16$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x = 14$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x = 7$. Check: with $x = 7$ both sides equal $44$. The wrong choices come from multiplying only some terms: $\frac{15}{2}$ forgets to multiply the 1 by 2, and $1$ forgets to multiply the 4 by 4.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $7x - 3 = -x + 21$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $8x = 24$. Divide both sides by $8$: $x = 3$. Check: with $x = 3$ both sides equal $18$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.stem: Which equation is equivalent to $4x + 5 - x = 2x - 9 + 6x$ after combining like terms on each side?
questions.solution: Left side: $4x - x = 3x$, so it is $3x + 5$. Right side: $2x + 6x = 8x$, so it is $8x - 9$. The equation is $3x + 5 = 8x - 9$. The other choices add $4x$ and $x$, change the sign of 9, or leave out the $-x$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: Solve: $\frac{2}{3}x - 4 = \frac{1}{6}x + 5$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $\frac{1}{2}x = 9$. Divide both sides by $\frac{1}{2}$: $x = 18$. Check: with $x = 18$ both sides equal $8$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $1.2x = 6$. Divide both sides by $1.2$: $x = 5$. Check: with $x = 5$ both sides equal $5.1$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: Which equation is equivalent to $\frac{x}{4} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{x}{2} - 1$ and has no fractions?
questions.solution: Multiply every term on both sides by 4: $4 \cdot \frac{x}{4} = x$, $4 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 2$, $4 \cdot \frac{x}{2} = 2x$ and $4 \cdot (-1) = -4$. The result is $x + 2 = 2x - 4$. The other choices forget to multiply a term by 4 or multiply a term by the wrong amount.

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: Solve $2(x + 3) = 2x + 5$ and decide how many solutions it has.
questions.answer: No solution
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $2x + 6 = 2x + 5$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = -1$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is never true, so there is no solution.

solve.answer: No solution

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: Which statement about $4x + 8 = 4(x + 2)$ is true?
choices: It is true for every value of $x$
It is true for exactly one value of $x$
It is true for no value of $x$
It is true for exactly two values of $x$
questions.answer: It is true for every value of $x$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $4x + 8 = 4x + 8$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = 0$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is always true, so every number is a solution.

solve.answer: It is true for every value of $x$

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: How many solutions does the equation $7x + 2 = 5x + 2$ have?
questions.answer: Exactly one solution
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x = 0$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x = 0$. Check: with $x = 0$ both sides equal $2$. The only solution is $x = 0$, so there is exactly one solution (the constants match, but the $x$ terms do not).

solve.answer: Exactly one solution

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: For what value of $k$ does $5x + k = 5(x - 3)$ have infinitely many solutions?
questions.solution: Expand the right side: $5(x - 3) = 5x - 15$. The equation $5x + k = 5x - 15$ is true for every $x$ exactly when $k = -15$.

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: The equation $4x - 9 = 4x + m$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $m$?
questions.solution: Both sides have $4x$. For the equation to be true for every $x$, the numbers must match too, so $m = -9$. With any other value of $m$ the equation has no solution.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: A rectangle has length $x + 6$ and width 3. A square has side length $x$. Which equation says that the rectangle and the square have the same perimeter?
questions.solution: The perimeter of the rectangle is twice the length plus twice the width: $2(x + 6) + 2(3)$. The perimeter of the square is $4x$. So the equation is $2(x + 6) + 2(3) = 4x$. The other choices find an area, add each side once, or count the width only once.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: A candle 20 cm tall burns down 2 cm each hour. A second candle 15 cm tall burns down 1 cm each hour. Let $h$ be the number of hours. Which equation says that the two candles are the same height?
questions.solution: After $h$ hours the first candle is $20 - 2h$ cm tall and the second is $15 - h$ cm tall. Setting them equal gives $20 - 2h = 15 - h$. The candles get shorter, so the terms with $h$ are subtracted.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: Plan A costs 15 dollars a month plus 0.10 dollars for each text. Plan B costs 5 dollars a month plus 0.20 dollars for each text. For how many texts in a month do the two plans cost the same?
questions.solution: For $t$ texts, Plan A costs $15 + 0.10t$ dollars and Plan B costs $5 + 0.20t$ dollars. Set them equal: $15 + 0.10t = 5 + 0.20t$. Then $10 = 0.10t$, so $t = 100$. Check: $15 + 10 = 25$ and $5 + 20 = 25$.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: Pool X has 100 liters and is filled at 20 liters per minute. Pool Y has 300 liters and is filled at 10 liters per minute. After how many minutes do the two pools hold the same amount?
questions.solution: After $m$ minutes the pools hold $100 + 20m$ and $300 + 10m$ liters. Setting them equal: $10m = 200$, so $m = 20$ minutes. Check: $100 + 400 = 500$ and $300 + 200 = 500$.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which inequality is equivalent to $8x - 5 \ge 3x + 20$?
questions.answer: $x \ge 5$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $5x \ge 25$. Divide both sides by $5$: $x \ge 5$. The other choices reverse the sign, move the 5 the wrong way, or add the $x$ terms.

solve.answer: $x \ge 5$

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What is the smallest integer $x$ that satisfies $9 + 5x > 2x - 6$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $5x + 9 > 2x - 6$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $3x > -15$. Divide both sides by $3$: $x > -5$. Since $x$ must be greater than $-5$, the smallest integer is $-4$. (Check: $9 + 5(-4) = -11 > 2(-4) - 6 = -14$.)

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: What is the least integer $x$ that satisfies $4 - 3x < 2x + 19$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-3x + 4 < 2x + 19$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-5x < 15$. Divide both sides by $-5$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x > -3$. Since $x$ must be greater than $-3$, the least integer is $-2$. (Check: $4 - 3(-2) = 10 < 2(-2) + 19 = 15$.)

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: Which inequality shows all of the solutions of $10 - 4x \le 6x - 20$?
questions.answer: $x \ge 3$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-4x + 10 \le 6x - 20$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-10x \le -30$. Divide both sides by $-10$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x \ge 3$. The other choices forget to reverse the sign or make a sign error with the numbers.

solve.answer: $x \ge 3$

questions.skill: Write an inequality for a situation
questions.stem: Ava has 100 dollars and spends 6 dollars each week. Ben has 40 dollars and saves 4 dollars each week. Let $w$ be the number of weeks. Which inequality says that Ava still has more money than Ben?
questions.solution: After $w$ weeks Ava has $100 - 6w$ dollars (she spends) and Ben has $40 + 4w$ dollars (he saves). "More than" means $>$. The other choices mix up who spends and who saves, or use the wrong sign.

questions.skill: Write an inequality for a situation
questions.stem: Which sentence matches the inequality $2n - 7 > n + 4$?
choices: 7 more than twice a number is greater than 4 more than the number
7 less than twice a number is greater than 4 less than the number
7 less than twice a number is less than 4 more than the number
7 less than twice a number is greater than 4 more than the number
questions.answer: 7 less than twice a number is greater than 4 more than the number
questions.solution: $2n - 7$ is 7 less than twice a number, $n + 4$ is 4 more than the number, and $>$ means "is greater than". The other choices change "less" to "more", change "more" to "less", or reverse the comparison.

solve.answer: 7 less than twice a number is greater than 4 more than the number
solve.work: 2n - 7 is 7 less than twice n; n + 4 is 4 more than n; > is greater than.

questions.skill: Name or count the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality
questions.stem: How many integers from $-5$ to $5$, including both $-5$ and $5$, satisfy $2x + 1 > 4x - 5$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-2x > -6$. Divide both sides by $-2$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x < 3$. The integers from $-5$ to $5$ that are less than 3 are $-5, -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2$, which is 8 integers.

questions.skill: Name or count the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality
questions.stem: What is the sum of all of the positive integers that satisfy $3x + 4 \le 2x + 9$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $x \le 5$. The positive integers that are 5 or less are 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, and their sum is 15.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: Li solved $2(x - 4) = x + 3$. Step 1: $2x - 4 = x + 3$. Step 2: $x = 7$. Where is her first mistake?
choices: Step 1; the 4 was not multiplied by 2
Step 2; $x$ should have been subtracted from the right side only
Step 1; 2 should have been added to $x - 4$
questions.answer: Step 1; the 4 was not multiplied by 2
questions.solution: In Step 1 the 2 must multiply both terms in the parentheses: $2(x - 4) = 2x - 8$, not $2x - 4$. The correct work is $2x - 8 = x + 3$, so $x = 11$. Step 2 is correct for the equation she wrote, but that equation was wrong.

solve.answer: Step 1; the 4 was not multiplied by 2
solve.work: 2(x - 4) = 2x - 8, not 2x - 4. Step 1 is the first mistake (correct x = 11).

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: Omar solved $-3x + 4 < 10$. Step 1: $-3x < 6$. Step 2: $x < -2$. What mistake did he make?
choices: In Step 1, he should have added 4 to both sides
In Step 2, he should have written $x < 2$
In Step 2, he did not reverse the inequality sign when dividing by $-3$
questions.answer: In Step 2, he did not reverse the inequality sign when dividing by $-3$
questions.solution: Step 1 is correct (subtract 4 from both sides). In Step 2 he divided both sides by $-3$, which reverses the inequality, so the answer is $x > -2$. (Check: $x = 0$ gives $4 < 10$, which is true, and $0 > -2$.)

solve.answer: In Step 2, he did not reverse the inequality sign when dividing by $-3$
solve.work: Step 1 correct: -3x < 6. Dividing by -3 must reverse: x > -2. He kept <.

questions.skill: Check a solution and justify the steps
questions.stem: Which property justifies the step from $3(x + 2) = 9$ to $3x + 6 = 9$?
questions.answer: The distributive property
questions.solution: The 3 outside the parentheses is multiplied by each term inside: $3(x + 2) = 3 \cdot x + 3 \cdot 2 = 3x + 6$. That is the distributive property.

solve.answer: The distributive property

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction coefficients on both sides
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $\frac{1}{2}x + 3 = \frac{1}{4}x + 8$
questions.solution: Subtract $\frac{1}{4}x$ from both sides: $\frac{1}{4}x + 3 = 8$. Subtract 3: $\frac{1}{4}x = 5$. Multiply by 4: $x = 20$. Check: $\frac{1}{2}(20) + 3 = 13$ and $\frac{1}{4}(20) + 8 = 13$.

questions.skill: Find the constant that gives infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: The equation $3(2x - 4) = 6x + k$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $k$?
questions.solution: Distribute on the left: $6x - 12 = 6x + k$. The $x$ terms already match. The equation is true for every $x$ only when the constants match too, so $k = -12$.

solve.work: 3(2x - 4) = 6x - 12. For infinitely many solutions 6x - 12 = 6x + k for all x, so k = -12. Any other k gives no solution.

questions.skill: Use an equation with the variable on both sides to solve a problem
questions.stem: Gym A charges 20 dollars to join plus 8 dollars for each visit. Gym B charges 50 dollars to join plus 5 dollars for each visit. After how many visits is the total cost the same at both gyms?
questions.solution: Let $v$ be the number of visits. Gym A costs $20 + 8v$ and Gym B costs $50 + 5v$. Set them equal: $20 + 8v = 50 + 5v$. Subtract $5v$: $20 + 3v = 50$. Subtract 20: $3v = 30$. So $v = 10$. Check: both cost 100 dollars.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $7x - 3 = 2x + 4$
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $5x = 7$. Divide both sides by $5$: $x = \frac{7}{5}$. Check: with $x = \frac{7}{5}$ both sides equal $\frac{34}{5}$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What is the solution of $-5x - 8 = -9x + 28$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $4x = 36$. Divide both sides by $4$: $x = 9$. Check: with $x = 9$ both sides equal $-53$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $6x - 8 = 2x + 16$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $4x = 24$. Divide both sides by $4$: $x = 6$. Check: with $x = 6$ both sides equal $28$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation that needs the distributive property
questions.stem: Find the solution of $-3(2x + 1) = 4(x - 2) - 5$.
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-6x - 3 = 4x - 13$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-10x = -10$. Divide both sides by $-10$: $x = 1$. Check: with $x = 1$ both sides equal $-9$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $4x + 14 = 6x - 12$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-2x = -26$. Divide both sides by $-2$: $x = 13$. Check: with $x = 13$ both sides equal $66$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation after combining like terms
questions.stem: Find the value of $x$: $4x - 9 + 3x - 2x = 15 - 3x + 6$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $5x - 9 = -3x + 21$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $8x = 30$. Divide both sides by $8$: $x = \frac{15}{4}$. Check: with $x = \frac{15}{4}$ both sides equal $\frac{39}{4}$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.stem: Solve for $x$: $\frac{3x - 1}{4} = \frac{x + 5}{2}$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{2}$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $\frac{1}{4}x = \frac{11}{4}$. Divide both sides by $\frac{1}{4}$: $x = 11$. Check: with $x = 11$ both sides equal $8$.

questions.skill: Solve an equation with fraction or decimal coefficients
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $0.25x + 2 = 0.5x - 1$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-0.25x = -3$. Divide both sides by $-0.25$: $x = 12$. Check: with $x = 12$ both sides equal $5$.

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: Which statement about $3(2x - 4) = 2(3x - 6)$ is true?
choices: It is true for exactly one value of $x$
It is true for no value of $x$
It is true for every value of $x$
It is true for exactly two values of $x$
questions.answer: It is true for every value of $x$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $6x - 12 = 6x - 12$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = 0$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is always true, so every number is a solution.

solve.answer: It is true for every value of $x$

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: After simplifying, how many solutions does $5(x - 2) + 3 = 5x - 6$ have?
questions.answer: No solution
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $5x - 7 = 5x - 6$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $0 = 1$. The $x$ terms cancel and what is left is never true, so there is no solution.

solve.answer: No solution

questions.skill: Decide whether an equation has one, no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: Which of these equations has no solution?
questions.solution: $2x + 6 = 2(x + 4)$ simplifies to $2x + 6 = 2x + 8$, which is never true, so it has no solution. $2x + 6 = 2(x + 3)$ is always true, $2x + 6 = 3x + 6$ gives $x = 0$, and $2x + 6 = 6 - 2x$ also gives $x = 0$.

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: For what value of $a$ does $ax + 5 = 3x - 2$ have no solution?
questions.solution: No solution happens when the $x$ terms cancel and the leftover numbers are different. If $a = 3$, the equation becomes $3x + 5 = 3x - 2$, which simplifies to $5 = -2$, never true. For any other $a$ there is exactly one solution.

solve.work: No solution needs equal x-coefficients and different constants: a = 3 gives 5 = -2, false.

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: The equation $a(x + 2) = 5x + 10$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: Expand the left side: $a(x + 2) = ax + 2a$. To match $5x + 10$ exactly, $a = 5$ and $2a = 10$. Both are true when $a = 5$.

questions.skill: Find the value that gives no or infinitely many solutions
questions.stem: The equation $2(3x + k) = ax + 14$ has infinitely many solutions. What is the value of $a + k$?
questions.solution: Expand the left side: $2(3x + k) = 6x + 2k$. To match $ax + 14$ exactly, $a = 6$ and $2k = 14$, so $k = 7$. Then $a + k = 6 + 7 = 13$.

solve.work: 6x + 2k = ax + 14 for all x: a = 6, 2k = 14 so k = 7; a + k = 13.

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: Jon is $j$ years old. His uncle is 20 years older than Jon. In 4 years, the uncle's age will be three times Jon's age at that time. Which equation represents this?
questions.solution: In 4 years the uncle will be $j + 20 + 4$ years old and Jon will be $j + 4$. The uncle's age is three times Jon's, so $j + 20 + 4 = 3(j + 4)$. The other choices forget that the uncle ages 4 years, forget that Jon ages 4 years, or ignore Jon's age entirely on the right.

solve.work: Uncle now j + 20, in 4 years j + 24; Jon then j + 4. j + 20 + 4 = 3(j + 4).

questions.skill: Write an equation for a situation
questions.stem: Three consecutive integers have a sum that is 9 less than five times the smallest integer. Let $n$ be the smallest integer. Which equation represents this?
questions.solution: The three integers are $n$, $n + 1$ and $n + 2$. Their sum is $n + (n + 1) + (n + 2)$. "9 less than five times the smallest" is $5n - 9$. So the equation is $n + (n + 1) + (n + 2) = 5n - 9$. The other choices add 9, subtract $5n$ from 9, or subtract 9 before multiplying.

solve.work: Sum n + (n+1) + (n+2); 9 less than five times the smallest: 5n - 9.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: A shop rents bikes for 12 dollars plus 4 dollars per hour. A second shop rents bikes for 5 dollars plus 6 dollars per hour. The two shops charge the same amount for a certain number of hours. What is that amount, in dollars?
questions.solution: For $h$ hours the shops charge $12 + 4h$ and $5 + 6h$. Set them equal: $7 = 2h$, so $h = 3.5$ hours. The charge is $12 + 4(3.5) = 26$ dollars, and $5 + 6(3.5) = 26$ dollars too.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: Jar A holds 3 times as many marbles as Jar B. After 10 marbles are taken out of Jar A and 6 marbles are put into Jar B, the two jars hold the same number of marbles. How many marbles did Jar A hold at the start?
questions.solution: Let Jar B start with $b$ marbles, so Jar A starts with $3b$. After the change: $3b - 10 = b + 6$. Then $2b = 16$, so $b = 8$ and Jar A started with $3 \cdot 8 = 24$ marbles. Check: $24 - 10 = 14$ and $8 + 6 = 14$.

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: A square has sides of length $2x + 1$. An equilateral triangle has sides of length $3x - 4$. The square and the triangle have the same perimeter. What is the perimeter of the square?
questions.solution: The square's perimeter is $4(2x + 1)$ and the triangle's is $3(3x - 4)$. Set them equal: $8x + 4 = 9x - 12$, so $x = 16$. The square's sides are $2(16) + 1 = 33$, so its perimeter is $4 \cdot 33 = 132$. (The triangle's sides are $3(16) - 4 = 44$ and $3 \cdot 44 = 132$.)

questions.skill: Solve a problem with an equation
questions.stem: A rectangle has a length that is 3 more than twice its width. If the width is increased by 5 and the length is decreased by 4, the new rectangle is a square. What is the width of the original rectangle?
questions.solution: Let the width be $w$. The length is $2w + 3$. The new width is $w + 5$ and the new length is $2w + 3 - 4$. A square has equal sides: $w + 5 = 2w + 3 - 4$, which gives $w + 5 = 2w - 1$ and $w = 6$. Check: the length was 15, the new sides are $11$ and $11$.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: Which inequality is equivalent to $2(3x - 1) \le 4x + 10$?
questions.answer: $x \le 6$
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $6x - 2 \le 4x + 10$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $2x \le 12$. Divide both sides by $2$: $x \le 6$. The other choices change the sign of the 2, reverse the inequality, or forget to multiply $3x$ by 2.

solve.answer: $x \le 6$

questions.skill: Solve an inequality with the variable on both sides
questions.stem: What is the least integer that satisfies $\frac{x}{2} + 3 \ge \frac{x}{4} + 5$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $\frac{1}{2}x + 3 \ge \frac{1}{4}x + 5$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $\frac{1}{4}x \ge 2$. Divide both sides by $\frac{1}{4}$: $x \ge 8$. So $x$ is 8 or greater, and the least integer is 8.

solve.work: x/2 - x/4 >= 2 -> x/4 >= 2 -> x >= 8; least integer 8.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: What is the greatest integer $x$ that satisfies $3(2 - x) > 5x + 38$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-3x + 6 > 5x + 38$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-8x > 32$. Divide both sides by $-8$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x < -4$. Since $x$ must be less than $-4$, the greatest integer is $-5$. (Check: $3(2 - (-5)) = 33 > 5(-5) + 38 = 13$.)

solve.work: 6 - 3x > 5x + 38 -> -32 > 8x -> x < -4; greatest integer -5. Check x=-5: 21 > -2 true; x=-4: 18 > 18 false.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: Which inequality shows all of the solutions of $-\frac{1}{2}x + 3 < x - 6$?
questions.solution: Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-\frac{3}{2}x < -9$. Divide both sides by $-\frac{3}{2}$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x > 6$. The other choices forget to reverse the sign, divide incorrectly, or combine the $x$ terms with the wrong sign.

questions.skill: Solve an inequality that needs a sign reversal
questions.stem: The solutions of $7 - 5x > 3(x - 3) + 4$ are all of the values of $x$ that are less than a certain number. What is that number?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $-5x + 7 > 3x - 5$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-8x > -12$. Divide both sides by $-8$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x < \frac{3}{2}$. So $x$ is less than $\frac{3}{2}$, and the number is $\frac{3}{2}$, or 1.5.

questions.skill: Write an inequality for a situation
questions.stem: A rectangle has length $3x$ and width 5. A square has side length $x + 6$. Which inequality says that the rectangle's perimeter is greater than the square's perimeter?
questions.solution: The rectangle's perimeter is $2(3x) + 2(5)$. The square's perimeter is $4(x + 6)$. "Greater than" means $>$. The other choices add each side only once, forget to multiply the 6 by 4, or count the width only once.

questions.skill: Name or count the whole numbers that satisfy an inequality
questions.stem: Which value of $x$ is NOT a solution of $2(x + 3) \le 5x - 9$?
questions.solution: Simplify each side: $2x + 6 \le 5x - 9$. Move the $x$ terms to one side and the numbers to the other: $-3x \le -15$. Divide both sides by $-3$. Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality: $x \ge 5$. So the solutions are 5 and greater. The value 4 is not a solution, since $2(4 + 3) = 14$ is not less than or equal to $5(4) - 9 = 11$.

solve.work: 2x + 6 <= 5x - 9 -> 15 <= 3x -> x >= 5. 4 is not a solution (14 <= 11 false); 5, 6, 10 are.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: Four students solved $4(x - 1) = 2x + 6$. Whose work is completely correct?
questions.solution: Distribute: $4(x - 1) = 4x - 4$. Subtract $2x$ from both sides: $2x - 4 = 6$. Add 4: $2x = 10$, so $x = 5$. Check: $4(5 - 1) = 16$ and $2(5) + 6 = 16$. The other students forgot to multiply the 1 by 4, added the $x$ terms, or subtracted 4 instead of adding it.

questions.skill: Find the error in a solution
questions.stem: A student solves $2(x + 4) = 2x + 3$ and gets $8 = 3$. She writes "$x = 5$" because $8 - 3 = 5$. What should she conclude instead?
choices: The equation has no solution, because $8 = 3$ is never true
questions.answer: The equation has no solution, because $8 = 3$ is never true
questions.solution: Distributing gives $2x + 8 = 2x + 3$. Subtracting $2x$ from both sides leaves $8 = 3$, which is false no matter what $x$ is. So no value of $x$ works: the equation has no solution. The number 5 is just the difference of 8 and 3, not a solution.

solve.answer: The equation has no solution, because $8 = 3$ is never true

questions.skill: Check a solution and justify the steps
questions.stem: Which set of steps solves $7x - 9 = 4x + 6$ correctly?
choices: Add $4x$ to both sides, subtract 9 from both sides, then divide both sides by 11
Subtract $4x$ from both sides, subtract 9 from both sides, then divide both sides by 3
Subtract $4x$ from both sides, add 9 to both sides, then divide both sides by 11
Subtract $4x$ from both sides, add 9 to both sides, then divide both sides by 3
questions.answer: Subtract $4x$ from both sides, add 9 to both sides, then divide both sides by 3
questions.solution: Subtract $4x$: $3x - 9 = 6$. Add 9: $3x = 15$. Divide by 3: $x = 5$. The other choices add $4x$ (which gives $11x - 9 = 8x + 6$), subtract 9 when it should be added, or divide by 11 when the coefficient of $x$ is 3.

solve.answer: Subtract $4x$ from both sides, add 9 to both sides, then divide both sides by 3

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of input-output pairs is a function
questions.stem: Each pair below is written as (input, output). Which set of pairs is a function?
questions.solution: A function gives exactly one output for each input. In the first set every input appears once. In the other sets an input is repeated with two different outputs: 1 gives 4 and 5, 2 gives 3 and 5, and 5 gives 1 and 4.

solve.work: A repeats input 2 with outputs 3 and 5; B repeats input 1; D repeats input 5. C has inputs 1,2,3,4 each once, so it is a function.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output
questions.stem: A function's rule is: the output is 3 more than twice the input. What is the output when the input is 5?
questions.solution: Twice the input is $2 \times 5 = 10$. Three more than that is $10 + 3 = 13$.

questions.skill: Describe how a quantity changes as time passes
questions.stem: A candle is measured at 0, 1, 2 and 3 hours. Its heights are 20, 17, 14 and 11 centimeters. Which statement describes the height as time goes on?
choices: The height increases by 3 centimeters each hour
The height decreases by 20 centimeters each hour
The height decreases by 3 centimeters each hour
The height decreases by 11 centimeters each hour
questions.answer: The height decreases by 3 centimeters each hour
questions.solution: Each hour the height goes from 20 to 17 to 14 to 11. It drops by 3 centimeters every hour, so the function is decreasing.

solve.answer: The height decreases by 3 centimeters each hour
solve.work: 20 -> 17 -> 14 -> 11: each hour the height drops by 3 cm.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: Lena wrote four lists of (input, output) pairs. Only one of the lists is a function. Which one is it?
questions.solution: A function gives every input exactly one output. In the list $(1, 7), (2, 7), (3, 7)$ the inputs 1, 2 and 3 each have one output; it does not matter that the output 7 is used three times. In each other list one input has two outputs: 1 goes to 2 and 3, 2 goes to 6 and 9, and 5 goes to 1 and 3.

solve.work: A: input 5 has outputs 1 and 3, not a function. B: inputs 1,2,3 each once (same output 7 is allowed), function. C: input 1 -> 2 and 3, not. D: input 2 -> 6 and 9, not. Only B.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: A table shows an input $x$ and an output $y$. When $x$ is 1, $y$ is 3. When $x$ is 2, $y$ is 5. When $x$ is 2, $y$ is 6. Why is this table not a function?
choices: The input 2 is paired with two different outputs
The outputs 3, 5 and 6 are all different from each other
The input 1 is paired with only one output
The output 5 is smaller than the output 6
questions.answer: The input 2 is paired with two different outputs
questions.solution: In a function each input has exactly one output. Here the input 2 has both 5 and 6, so the table is not a function. The other statements are true, but they do not break the rule.

solve.answer: The input 2 is paired with two different outputs
solve.work: Input 2 is paired with both 5 and 6, so the table fails the one-output-per-input rule. The other reasons are irrelevant.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: Sam wrote three relations as (input, output) pairs. Relation A: $(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4)$. Relation B: $(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4)$. Relation C: $(5, 0), (6, 0), (7, 0)$. How many of the three relations are functions?
questions.solution: Relation A is a function: each input has one output. Relation B is not, because the input 1 has the outputs 2 and 3. Relation C is a function: each input has the output 0, and repeating an output is allowed. So 2 of the relations are functions.

solve.work: A: inputs 1,2,3 distinct, function. B: input 1 -> 2 and 3, not. C: inputs 5,6,7 distinct (repeated output 0 is fine), function. 2 functions.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: A set of (input, output) pairs is a function. Which statement must be true?
choices: No output is used more than once
No input is paired with two different outputs
Every output is greater than its input
The inputs are listed from least to greatest
questions.answer: No input is paired with two different outputs
questions.solution: The rule for a function is that each input has exactly one output. Outputs may repeat, they need not be larger than the inputs, and the pairs need not be in order.

solve.answer: No input is paired with two different outputs
solve.work: Definition of a function: each input has exactly one output, so no input is paired with two different outputs. Order, repeated outputs and size are not required.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: Which of these relationships is a function from the first quantity to the second?
choices: Input: a student. Output: that student's date of birth.
Input: a school. Output: a student at that school.
Input: a state. Output: a city in that state.
Input: a month. Output: a student born in that month.
questions.answer: Input: a student. Output: that student's date of birth.
questions.solution: Every student has exactly one date of birth, so each input has one output. A school has many students, a state has many cities, and many students can be born in the same month, so those are not functions.

solve.answer: Input: a student. Output: that student's date of birth.
solve.work: A state has many cities; a month has many students born in it; a school has many students. A student has exactly one date of birth, so student -> date of birth is a function.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: A bakery sells muffins for 2 dollars each. A table shows that 1 muffin costs 2 dollars, 2 muffins cost 4 dollars and 3 muffins cost 6 dollars. For the input 3 muffins, how many different prices (outputs) are there?
questions.solution: Three muffins cost 6 dollars and no other price, so the input 3 has exactly 1 output. That is what makes the cost a function of the number of muffins.

solve.issues: Very easy for grade 8, but correct and on the function idea.
solve.work: The muffin price is a function: 3 muffins cost 3 x 2 = 6 dollars, a single price. Number of different outputs for input 3 is 1.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: In which pair is the second quantity a function of the first?
choices: First: a person's age. Second: that person's height.
First: a team name. Second: a player on that team.
First: a color. Second: a car of that color.
First: the number of tickets bought at 6 dollars each. Second: the total cost.
questions.answer: First: the number of tickets bought at 6 dollars each. Second: the total cost.
questions.solution: Each number of tickets gives exactly one total cost, so the cost is a function of the number of tickets. People of the same age can have different heights, a team has many players, and many cars can share a color.

solve.answer: First: the number of tickets bought at 6 dollars each. Second: the total cost.
solve.work: Team -> player: many players. Age -> height: people of the same age have different heights. Colour -> car: many cars. Tickets -> total cost: cost = 6 x tickets, exactly one value. Answer C.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A function machine takes a number, multiplies it by 4 and gives the result. What does it output for the input 7?
questions.solution: The machine multiplies by 4: $4 \times 7 = 28$.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A function is given by $y = 5x - 2$. What is $y$ when $x = 4$?
questions.solution: Put $x = 4$ into the rule: $5 \times 4 - 2 = 20 - 2 = 18$.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A function's rule is: the output is the input divided by 2. Which pair (input, output) fits this rule?
questions.solution: Divide the input by 2: $10 \div 2 = 5$, so the pair is $(10, 5)$. The pair $(10, 20)$ multiplies by 2, $(10, 8)$ subtracts 2 and $(10, 12)$ adds 2.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: A puppy's weight is measured at ages 1, 2, 3 and 4 months. The weights are 5, 8, 12 and 15 pounds. Which describes the weight as the age goes up?
choices: It goes up and then goes down
questions.answer: It is increasing
questions.solution: Each weight is greater than the one before (5, 8, 12, 15), so the weight keeps going up as the age goes up. The function is increasing.

solve.answer: It is increasing

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: As the outside temperature goes up, the number of hot drinks a cafe sells goes down. How does the number of hot drinks sold change as the temperature increases?
choices: It goes down and then goes up
questions.answer: It is decreasing
questions.solution: When the input (temperature) goes up, the output (hot drinks sold) goes down. A function like that is decreasing.

solve.answer: It is decreasing
solve.work: Higher temperature -> fewer hot drinks: decreasing.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: A function has the outputs 12, 9, 6, 3 and 0 for the inputs 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. What is the change in the output each time the input goes up by 1? Use a negative number if the output goes down.
questions.solution: Each output is 3 less than the one before: $9 - 12 = -3$. The change is $-3$, which shows a decreasing function.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: Which statement describes a decreasing function?
choices: As the input gets larger, the output stays the same
As the input gets smaller, the output gets smaller
As the input gets larger, the output gets smaller
The output is always a negative number
questions.answer: As the input gets larger, the output gets smaller
questions.solution: A decreasing function has outputs that go down as the inputs go up. An output that stays the same describes a constant function, an output that gets smaller as the input gets smaller describes an increasing function, and a decreasing function can still have positive outputs.

solve.answer: As the input gets larger, the output gets smaller
solve.work: Decreasing: as input increases, output decreases. Option D describes increasing; A and B are not decreasing.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: The temperature at 6 AM, 7 AM, 8 AM, 9 AM and 10 AM was 50, 54, 53, 59 and 63 degrees. Over how many of the four one-hour steps did the temperature increase?
questions.solution: Compare each hour with the one before. 50 to 54 goes up, 54 to 53 goes down, 53 to 59 goes up and 59 to 63 goes up. The temperature increased in 3 of the 4 steps.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: Imagine the graph of the depth of the water in a pool. The pool is filled for 3 hours, stays full for 2 hours, and is then emptied for 3 hours (hours 0 to 8). During which hours is the depth decreasing?
questions.answer: From hour 5 to hour 8
questions.solution: The depth goes up during the first 3 hours, stays the same from hour 3 to hour 5, and goes down from hour 5 to hour 8 while the pool is emptied.

solve.answer: From hour 5 to hour 8

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: The money in a jar was 10 dollars in week 0, 14 dollars in week 1, 14 dollars in week 2 and 8 dollars in week 3. Over which one-week step did the amount decrease?
questions.answer: From week 2 to week 3
questions.solution: From week 0 to week 1 the amount goes up (10 to 14), from week 1 to week 2 it stays the same (14 to 14), and from week 2 to week 3 it goes down (14 to 8).

solve.answer: From week 2 to week 3
solve.work: 10->14 up, 14->14 same, 14->8 down. Week 2 to week 3. (Week 0 to 2 is not a one-week step and is a rise.)

questions.skill: Tell linear from non-linear using pairs or a table
questions.stem: A function has the outputs 4, 7, 10 and 13 for the inputs 0, 1, 2 and 3. By how much does the output go up each time the input goes up by 1?
questions.solution: Each output is 3 more than the one before: $7 - 4 = 3$, $10 - 7 = 3$ and $13 - 10 = 3$. The output goes up by 3 each time, so the function is linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from non-linear using pairs or a table
questions.stem: A function has the inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4. Which list of outputs makes it a linear function?
questions.solution: A linear function changes by the same amount for every step of 1 in the input. The outputs 2, 4, 6, 8 go up by 2 each time. The other lists go up by 2, 4, 8; by 3, 5, 7; and by 1, 2, 3.

questions.skill: Tell linear from non-linear using an equation or a description
questions.stem: Which of these equations has a straight-line graph?
questions.solution: An equation of the form $y = mx + b$ has a straight-line graph, so $y = 2x + 3$ is linear. The equations with $x^2$, $2^x$ and $x^3$ have curved graphs.

solve.work: x^3 - 1, 2^x and x^2 are curves; y = 2x + 3 is linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from non-linear using an equation or a description
questions.stem: Which situation is described by a linear function?
choices: A bank balance doubles every year
The area of a square as its side length grows
A tree grows exactly 3 inches every year
The height of a ball thrown into the air
questions.answer: A tree grows exactly 3 inches every year
questions.solution: A linear function changes by the same amount for each step. The tree's height goes up by 3 inches every year. A doubling balance, a growing square's area and the height of a thrown ball do not change by a constant amount.

solve.answer: A tree grows exactly 3 inches every year
solve.work: Thrown ball: rises then falls (curve). Doubling balance: exponential. Square area: s^2. A tree growing exactly 3 inches each year: constant rate, linear.

questions.skill: Tell linear from non-linear using an equation or a description
questions.stem: The graph of $y = 6x - 1$ is a straight line. By how much does $y$ increase when $x$ increases by 1?
questions.solution: In $y = mx + b$, the output changes by $m$ for each increase of 1 in $x$. Here $m = 6$, so $y$ increases by 6.

solve.work: Slope 6: y increases by 6 for each 1 in x.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: Water is poured into a bucket at a steady rate. Imagine the graph of the depth of the water against time. Which describes the graph?
choices: A straight line that goes down from left to right
A curve that goes up and then comes down
A straight line that goes up from left to right
questions.answer: A straight line that goes up from left to right
questions.solution: The depth increases by the same amount every second, so the graph is a straight line that rises as time goes on.

solve.answer: A straight line that goes up from left to right
solve.work: Steady rate: depth rises by equal amounts per unit time, a straight line rising left to right.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: A car is parked for two hours. Imagine the graph of its distance from home against time during those two hours. Which describes the graph?
choices: A straight line that goes up from left to right
A straight line that goes down from left to right
A curve that goes up and then comes down
questions.answer: A horizontal line
questions.solution: A parked car does not move, so its distance from home does not change. The graph stays at the same height: a horizontal line.

solve.answer: A horizontal line
solve.work: Parked: distance from home does not change, horizontal line.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: A ball is thrown straight up and then falls back to the ground. Imagine the graph of its height against time. Which describes the graph?
choices: It falls to a lowest point and then rises
It stays at the same height
It rises to a peak and then falls
It rises steadily and never falls
questions.answer: It rises to a peak and then falls
questions.solution: The ball goes up, reaches its highest point, and comes back down. The height rises to a peak and then falls.

solve.answer: It rises to a peak and then falls
solve.work: Height rises to a maximum and then falls back to the ground.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: Ava walks to a store for 10 minutes, stays inside for 15 minutes, and then walks home for 10 minutes. Imagine the graph of her distance from home against time. For how many minutes is the graph horizontal?
questions.solution: The graph is horizontal when her distance from home does not change. That is while she is inside the store, for 15 minutes.

solve.work: Distance constant while inside the store: 15 minutes.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: A bathtub is filled, stays full while someone bathes, and is then drained. Imagine the graph of the depth of the water against time. Which describes the graph, from left to right?
choices: It falls, stays flat, then rises
It rises, stays flat, then falls
It rises, falls, then stays flat
It stays flat, rises, then falls
questions.answer: It rises, stays flat, then falls
questions.solution: Filling makes the depth rise, bathing keeps it level, and draining makes it fall, in that order.

solve.answer: It rises, stays flat, then falls
solve.work: Filling: rises; full: flat; draining: falls.

questions.skill: Match a real situation to the shape of its graph
questions.stem: A plant grows 2 centimeters each week for 4 weeks and then stops growing for 2 weeks. Imagine the graph of its height against time. Which describes the graph, from left to right?
choices: A line that goes up, then goes down
A line that is horizontal, then goes up
A line that goes up, then becomes horizontal
A line that goes up steeply, then goes up less steeply
questions.answer: A line that goes up, then becomes horizontal
questions.solution: The height rises steadily for 4 weeks. When the plant stops growing, the height stays the same, so the graph becomes horizontal.

solve.answer: A line that goes up, then becomes horizontal
solve.work: Height rises 2 cm/week for 4 weeks (line up), then no growth (horizontal).

questions.skill: Describe the pattern of change in a non-linear function
questions.stem: The outputs of a function for the inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4 are 2, 4, 8 and 16. Each output is double the one before it. What is the output for the input 6?
questions.solution: Keep doubling: the input 5 gives $16 \times 2 = 32$ and the input 6 gives $32 \times 2 = 64$.

questions.skill: Describe the pattern of change in a non-linear function
questions.stem: A function has the outputs 1, 4, 9 and 16 for the inputs 1, 2, 3 and 4. How does the output change as the input goes up by 1 each time?
choices: It goes up by the same amount each time
It goes up by a smaller amount each time
It goes up by a larger amount each time
questions.answer: It goes up by a larger amount each time
questions.solution: The outputs go up by $4 - 1 = 3$, then $9 - 4 = 5$, then $16 - 9 = 7$. The amount of increase gets larger each time, so the function is not linear.

solve.answer: It goes up by a larger amount each time
solve.work: Differences 3, 5, 7: rises by a larger amount each time.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function from a list of pairs is linear
questions.stem: A function has these (input, output) pairs: (1, 2), (2, 5), (3, 10), (4, 17). Is the function linear?
choices: No, because the output does not change by the same amount each time
Yes, because the output always goes up
Yes, because the input goes up by 1 each time
Yes, because the output is always greater than the input
questions.answer: No, because the output does not change by the same amount each time
questions.solution: The outputs change by 3, then 5, then 7. A linear function changes by the same amount each time the input goes up by 1, so this function is not linear.

solve.answer: No, because the output does not change by the same amount each time
solve.work: Output changes: 2->5 (+3), 5->10 (+5), 10->17 (+7). Equal input steps but unequal output changes, so not linear (outputs are x^2 + 1).

questions.skill: Tell which relationship gives exactly one output for each input
questions.stem: Which relationship gives exactly one output for every input?
choices: Input: a letter of the alphabet. Output: a word that starts with that letter
Input: a whole number from 1 to 20. Output: a whole number that divides it evenly
Input: the side length of a square. Output: the area of that square
Input: a country. Output: a city in that country
questions.answer: Input: the side length of a square. Output: the area of that square
questions.solution: A square with a given side length has only one area, so this is a function. A letter can start many words, 12 is divided evenly by 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, and a country has many cities, so those inputs have more than one possible output.

solve.answer: Input: the side length of a square. Output: the area of that square
solve.work: A letter has many words; a number like 6 has divisors 1,2,3,6; a country has many cities. A square's side determines exactly one area (s^2). So C.

questions.skill: Find how long a quantity is decreasing
questions.stem: A hiker's height above sea level is measured every hour. At hours 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 the heights in meters are 100, 300, 500, 500, 300 and 100. For how many hours is the height decreasing?
questions.solution: The height rises from hour 0 to hour 2, stays at 500 from hour 2 to hour 3, and falls from hour 3 to hour 5 (500, then 300, then 100). It is decreasing for $5 - 3 = 2$ hours.

solve.work: Hours 0-1: up; 1-2: up; 2-3: level (500 to 500); 3-4: down; 4-5: down. Decreasing during 2 hours.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: In a function, the input 3 has the output 8. Which pair could also be in that same function?
questions.solution: The input 3 already has the output 8, so no other pair can start with 3. The pair $(5, 8)$ has a new input, 5, so it can be added.

solve.work: Input 3 already has output 8, so any other pair with input 3 and a different output breaks the function. (5, 8) uses a new input; a repeated output is allowed.

questions.skill: Tell whether a set of pairs is a function
questions.stem: These (input, output) pairs are listed: $(1, 3), (2, 5), (2, 6), (4, 7), (4, 8), (4, 9), (5, 1), (6, 2)$. How many different inputs are paired with more than one output?
questions.solution: Look at each input. The input 2 has the outputs 5 and 6. The input 4 has the outputs 7, 8 and 9. The inputs 1, 5 and 6 each have one output. So 2 inputs have more than one output.

solve.work: Input 1: 3. Input 2: 5, 6 (two). Input 4: 7, 8, 9 (three). Inputs 5, 6: one each. Inputs with more than one output: 2 and 4, so 2.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: The table shows the day of the month (the input) and the high temperature in degrees (the output): day 1, 70; day 2, 68; day 3, 70; day 4, 65. Which statement is correct?
choices: It is not a function, because 70 is the output for two different days
It is not a function, because the temperatures do not go up each day
It is a function, because each day has exactly one high temperature
It is not a function, because the temperature changes from day to day
questions.answer: It is a function, because each day has exactly one high temperature
questions.solution: Each day appears once, with one temperature. Two days may share the same output (70) and the outputs need not follow a pattern, so the table is a function.

solve.answer: It is a function, because each day has exactly one high temperature
solve.work: Each day 1-4 has exactly one high temperature; repeated output 70 for days 1 and 3 is allowed. So it is a function.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: A rule pairs each whole number input with each of its factors as outputs. For the input 12, how many outputs does the rule give?
questions.solution: The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. That is 6 outputs for the single input 12, so this rule is not a function.

questions.skill: Tell whether a situation or rule is a function
questions.stem: For positive whole number inputs, which rule gives every input exactly one output?
choices: The output is the number of digits in the input
The output is a multiple of the input
The output is a number larger than the input
The output is a factor of the input
questions.answer: The output is the number of digits in the input
questions.solution: A number has exactly one count of digits, so the first rule gives one output per input. An input such as 6 has many multiples (6, 12, 18, ...), many larger numbers, and several factors (1, 2, 3, 6).

solve.answer: The output is the number of digits in the input
solve.work: Multiples, larger numbers and factors each give many possible outputs (e.g. input 6 has factors 1,2,3,6). The number of digits of a positive whole number is a single value. Answer B.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A taxi charges 3 dollars to start and then 2 dollars for each mile. The cost in dollars of a ride of $m$ miles is $C = 3 + 2m$. What is the cost, in dollars, of a 9-mile ride?
questions.solution: Put $m = 9$ into the rule: $C = 3 + 2 \times 9 = 3 + 18 = 21$ dollars.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: The rule for a function is $y = 4x - 5$. For what input $x$ is the output 27?
questions.solution: Set $4x - 5 = 27$. Add 5: $4x = 32$. Divide by 4: $x = 8$.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A function is given by $y = x^2 + 1$. What is $y$ when $x = -3$?
questions.solution: Square first: $(-3)^2 = 9$, since a negative times a negative is positive. Then add 1: $9 + 1 = 10$.

questions.skill: Use a function rule to find an output or an input
questions.stem: A function has the rule $y = 10 - 3x$. For which input is the output $-2$?
questions.solution: Set $10 - 3x = -2$. Subtract 10: $-3x = -12$. Divide by $-3$: $x = 4$. Check: $10 - 3 \times 4 = -2$.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: Which equation describes a decreasing function?
questions.solution: In $y = -x + 8$ the output goes down by 1 each time $x$ goes up by 1. In the other three equations the number multiplying $x$ is positive, so the output goes up as $x$ goes up.

solve.work: Slopes: -1, 1/2, 3, 4. Only y = -x + 8 has a negative rate, so it decreases.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: Water in a tank is measured in liters. After 0, 1 and 2 hours the amounts are 400, 340 and 280, and the amount changes by the same amount each hour. What is the change in the amount of water each hour? Use a negative number if the amount goes down.
questions.solution: The amount after 1 hour minus the amount at the start is $340 - 400 = -60$. The amount of water changes by $-60$ liters each hour, so the function is decreasing.

questions.skill: Decide whether a function is increasing or decreasing
questions.stem: A function has the same output, 3, for each of the inputs 0, 1, 2 and 3. Which statement is correct?
choices: It is neither increasing nor decreasing
It is both increasing and decreasing
questions.answer: It is neither increasing nor decreasing
questions.solution: The output never goes up and never goes down, it stays at 3. So the function is constant: neither increasing nor decreasing.

solve.answer: It is neither increasing nor decreasing
solve.work: Constant output 3: it neither rises nor falls, so neither increasing nor decreasing.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: The outputs of a function for the inputs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 are 4, 7, 5, 9, 6, 6 and 3. Over how many of the 6 steps from one input to the next does the output decrease?
questions.solution: Compare each output with the one before. 4 to 7 up, 7 to 5 down, 5 to 9 up, 9 to 6 down, 6 to 6 no change, 6 to 3 down. The output decreases in 3 of the steps.

solve.work: 4->7 up, 7->5 down, 5->9 up, 9->6 down, 6->6 same, 6->3 down. 3 decreases.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: A ball's heights, in feet, at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 seconds are 0, 7, 12, 15, 16, 15, 12, 7 and 0. The height rises and then falls, with no other changes. During how many seconds is the height increasing?
questions.solution: The heights go up from 0 to 16 between 0 and 4 seconds, and then fall back to 0. The height is increasing for $4 - 0 = 4$ seconds.

solve.work: Heights rise 0,7,12,15,16 from t=0 to t=4, then fall. Increasing for 4 seconds.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: The outputs of a function for the inputs 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are 10, 8, 6, 6, 9, 12 and 15. On which interval of inputs is the function decreasing?
questions.answer: From input 0 to input 2
questions.solution: Between inputs 0 and 2 the outputs go 10, 8, 6, which is falling. From 2 to 3 the output stays at 6, and from 3 to 6 it rises (6, 9, 12, 15). The interval from 2 to 5 is flat and then rising.

solve.answer: From input 0 to input 2
solve.work: 10, 8, 6 for inputs 0-2 (falling), 6 to 6 flat (2-3), then rising 3-6. Decreasing on 0 to 2.

questions.skill: Find where a function increases or decreases
questions.stem: The outputs of a function for the inputs 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are 3, 6, 4, 4, 8 and 2. Which statement is true?
choices: It increases from input 3 to input 4
It decreases from input 1 to input 2
It decreases from input 2 to input 3 and from input 5 to input 6
It increases from input 5 to input 6
questions.answer: It decreases from input 2 to input 3 and from input 5 to input 6
questions.solution: From input 2 to 3 the output goes from 6 to 4, a decrease, and from input 5 to 6 it goes from 8 to 2, a decrease. From input 3 to 4 it stays at 4, from input 1 to 2 it rises from 3 to 6, and from input 5 to 6 it falls.

solve.answer: It decreases from input 2 to input 3 and from input 5 to input 6
