questions.solution: A fair question uses neutral wording. The other three questions use loaded words ("far too little", "terribly", "always too tired") that suggest the answer the writer expects.

solve.answer: How many hours do you usually sleep on a school night?
solve.work: The neutral question asks for hours without leading wording.

questions.skill: Recognize a statistical question
questions.stem: Here are five questions. (1) What is the typical number of text messages a teenager in our town sends each day? (2) How many text messages did Zoe send today? (3) How much does a ticket to the town fair cost? (4) How long do the students in each of four classes take to finish the same test? (5) What was the high temperature in our town yesterday? How many of the five are statistical questions?
questions.solution: Questions (1) and (4) ask about many people or classes, and the data will vary, so they are statistical. Questions (2), (3) and (5) each have a single answer. The answer is 2.

solve.work: (1) statistical, (2) one answer, (3) one price, (4) statistical, (5) one value. Count = 2.

questions.skill: Spot a biased or unclear survey question
questions.stem: Which survey question about a school's start time is least likely to bias the answers?
choices: Wouldn't you like school to start later so you can finally get enough sleep?
Most students want a later start. Do you want one too?
What start time would you prefer: 7:30, 8:00, 8:30 or 9:00?
Do you want school to start at the awful time of 7:30?
questions.answer: What start time would you prefer: 7:30, 8:00, 8:30 or 9:00?
questions.solution: The fair question gives a range of choices and no reason to pick one. The others suggest the "right" answer with phrases such as "finally get enough sleep", "most students want" and "awful".

solve.answer: What start time would you prefer: 7:30, 8:00, 8:30 or 9:00?
solve.work: Listing neutral time choices without loaded wording is least biased.

questions.skill: Identify bias in how a sample is chosen
questions.stem: A town has 8,000 residents. A phone poll that called only landline numbers found that 70% of those reached support a new tax. A random sample of residents, reached by both landline and cell phone, found that 55% support it. If the random sample is trusted, how many fewer residents support the tax than the landline poll suggests?
questions.solution: The landline poll suggests 70% of 8,000 = 5,600 residents. The random sample suggests 55% of 8,000 = 4,400 residents. The difference is 5,600 - 4,400 = 1,200 residents.

questions.skill: Identify and carry out random sampling
questions.stem: A systematic sample starts with student 4 on a list of 100 students and then takes every 6th student after that (4, 10, 16, and so on). How many students are in the sample?
questions.solution: The students chosen are 4, 10, 16, ..., 100. Each step adds 6, and (100 - 4) / 6 = 16 steps, so there are 16 + 1 = 17 students.

questions.skill: Identify and carry out random sampling
questions.stem: A random number generator is used to choose 5 students from a list numbered 1 to 60. It produces 17, 42, 17, 8, 63, 55, 31. Repeated numbers and numbers over 60 are skipped. What is the sum of the numbers of the five students chosen?
questions.solution: Skip the second 17 (a repeat) and 63 (over 60). The students chosen are 17, 42, 8, 55 and 31. Their sum is 17 + 42 + 8 + 55 + 31 = 153.

questions.skill: Design a simulation
questions.stem: One in 3 students at a school likes tea. Which tool can NOT be used to simulate choosing one student and seeing whether the student likes tea?
choices: A number cube, with a 1 or 2 meaning the student likes tea
A spinner with 3 equal sections, one labeled tea
A bag with 1 green marble and 2 red marbles, with green meaning tea
A fair coin, with heads meaning the student likes tea
questions.answer: A fair coin, with heads meaning the student likes tea
questions.solution: A coin gives a chance of 1 in 2. A cube with two favorable faces, a spinner with 1 of 3 equal sections and a bag with 1 of 3 marbles each give a chance of 1 in 3.

solve.answer: A fair coin, with heads meaning the student likes tea
solve.work: A coin gives 1/2, not 1/3. Cube 1-2 = 1/3, spinner 1 of 3, bag 1 of 3 all work.

questions.skill: Design a simulation
questions.stem: In a school, 25% of the students are in grade 6, 25% are in grade 7 and 50% are in grade 8. Random numbers from 1 to 20 are used to simulate choosing one student. Which assignment models this?
choices: 1 to 5 mean grade 6, 6 to 10 mean grade 7, and 11 to 15 mean grade 8
1 to 5 mean grade 6, 6 to 10 mean grade 7, and 11 to 20 mean grade 8
1 to 10 mean grade 6, 11 to 15 mean grade 7, and 16 to 20 mean grade 8
1 to 7 mean grade 6, 8 to 14 mean grade 7, and 15 to 20 mean grade 8
questions.answer: 1 to 5 mean grade 6, 6 to 10 mean grade 7, and 11 to 20 mean grade 8
questions.solution: 25% of 20 numbers is 5 numbers for grade 6, 5 numbers for grade 7 and 10 numbers for grade 8, which uses all 20 numbers. Giving grade 8 only 11 to 15 models just 25% for grade 8 and leaves 16 to 20 unassigned. Giving grade 6 the numbers 1 to 10 models 50% for grade 6, and the groups 7, 7 and 6 numbers model 35%, 35% and 30%.

solve.answer: 1 to 5 mean grade 6, 6 to 10 mean grade 7, and 11 to 20 mean grade 8

questions.skill: Design a simulation
questions.stem: At a school, 30% of the students are in grade 6, 30% are in grade 7 and 40% are in grade 8. In a simulation, the digits 0 to 2 stand for grade 6, the digits 3 to 5 for grade 7 and the digits 6 to 9 for grade 8. The simulation makes these 20 digits: 5 8 1 9 0 3 6 2 7 4 8 8 1 6 9 0 5 7 2 6. How many more of the simulated students are in grade 8 than in grade 6?
questions.solution: Grade 8 digits (6 to 9): 8, 9, 6, 7, 8, 8, 6, 9, 7, 6, which is 10 digits. Grade 6 digits (0 to 2): 1, 0, 2, 1, 0, 2, which is 6 digits. The difference is 10 - 6 = 4.

questions.skill: Estimate a probability from simulation results
questions.stem: In a population, 40% of the students like soccer. A simulation takes 20 random samples of 5 students. The numbers of students who like soccer in the 20 samples are 2, 3, 1, 2, 0, 4, 1, 2, 3, 2, 0, 1, 3, 2, 1, 2, 2, 3, 0, 5. In what fraction of the 20 samples did exactly 2 students like soccer?
questions.solution: Count the samples with exactly 2 students: 7 of the 20 samples. The fraction is 7/20.

questions.skill: Estimate a probability from simulation results
questions.stem: A simulation estimates that the chance a random sample of 8 students has 6 or more girls is 0.04. If 500 such random samples were taken, about how many would you expect to have 6 or more girls?
questions.solution: 0.04 of 500 samples is 0.04 x 500 = 20 samples.

questions.skill: Estimate a probability from simulation results
questions.stem: Simulation 1 has 40 trials and 14 of them are successes. Simulation 2 has 60 trials and 16 of them are successes. If the results of both simulations are combined, what is the estimated percent of trials that are successes?
questions.solution: Combined successes: 14 + 16 = 30. Combined trials: 40 + 60 = 100. The percent is 30 / 100 = 30%.

questions.skill: Judge whether a sample is valid for several populations
questions.stem: A proportional random sample of 60 students from a school includes 18 eighth graders. What percent of the school's students are in eighth grade?
questions.solution: In a proportional sample, the sample has the same share of eighth graders as the school. 18 / 60 = 0.3 = 30%.

solve.issues: Minor: "proportional random sample" is uncommon wording for Grade 8; as a plain random sample the result is only an estimate ("about 30%").

questions.skill: Organize and summarize data from several populations
questions.stem: The times, in minutes, that 7 students at each of two schools take to reach school are listed. Pine: 5, 25, 10, 15, 30, 10, 20. Oak: 12, 14, 9, 11, 15, 10, 13. How many minutes greater is the median time at Pine than the median time at Oak?
questions.solution: Pine in order: 5, 10, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, so the median is 15. Oak in order: 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, so the median is 12. The difference is 15 - 12 = 3 minutes.

solve.work: Pine sorted: 5,10,10,15,20,25,30 -> median 15. Oak sorted: 9,10,11,12,13,14,15 -> median 12. Difference 3.

questions.skill: Organize and summarize data from several populations
questions.stem: Test scores for three classes are listed. Class 1: 70, 85, 90, 75. Class 2: 60, 95, 80, 85. Class 3: 88, 90, 86, 92. What is the range of the class whose scores are the most spread out?
questions.solution: Class 1 range: 90 - 70 = 20. Class 2 range: 95 - 60 = 35. Class 3 range: 92 - 86 = 6. The greatest range is 35.

solve.work: Ranges: Class 1: 90 - 70 = 20. Class 2: 95 - 60 = 35. Class 3: 92 - 86 = 6. Most spread out is Class 2 (also largest MAD): 35.

questions.skill: Use random samples to predict for populations
questions.stem: A random sample of 40 students at School A shows that 14 have pets. A random sample of 60 students at School B shows that 15 have pets. School A has 800 students and School B has 1,200 students. About how many more students are predicted to have pets at School B than at School A?
questions.solution: School A: 14/40 = 35% of 800 = 280 students. School B: 15/60 = 25% of 1,200 = 300 students. School B has 300 - 280 = 20 more.

questions.skill: Use random samples to predict for populations
questions.stem: A random sample of 50 students from a school of 900 found 9 who are vegetarian. A second random sample of 100 students from the same school found 17 vegetarians. Combine the two samples to predict how many of the 900 students are vegetarian.
questions.solution: Combined, there are 9 + 17 = 26 vegetarians among 50 + 100 = 150 students. That is 26/150 of the students. Predict 26/150 x 900 = 156 students.

questions.skill: Recognize a statistical question
questions.stem: Which question is a statistical question?
choices: How old is the principal of Lake School, who has led the school for many years?
What is the typical age of the teachers who teach at Lake School this year?
How many students go to Lake School, including the new students this year?
What time does school start at Lake School on a normal weekday morning?
questions.answer: What is the typical age of the teachers who teach at Lake School this year?
questions.solution: The teachers at the school have different ages, so the data vary and the question asks for a typical value. The other questions each have one answer.

solve.answer: What is the typical age of the teachers who teach at Lake School this year?
solve.work: Typical age of teachers varies among teachers -> statistical. Others have a single answer.

questions.skill: Write a question that compares several populations
questions.stem: Which question names the populations and says what will be measured?
choices: Do kids who go to school in the middle grades do their homework when they get home from school?
How much homework is there for the students who go to school at Oak Middle School?
What do the students at Oak Middle School think about school, their teachers and their classes?
How many minutes per night do 6th, 7th and 8th graders at Oak Middle School spend on homework?
questions.answer: How many minutes per night do 6th, 7th and 8th graders at Oak Middle School spend on homework?
questions.solution: The question about 6th, 7th and 8th graders at Oak Middle School names three groups and the measurement (minutes per night on homework). The other questions are too vague.

solve.answer: How many minutes per night do 6th, 7th and 8th graders at Oak Middle School spend on homework?
solve.work: Names populations (6th, 7th, 8th graders at Oak MS) and measure (minutes per night on homework).

questions.skill: Write a question that compares several populations
questions.stem: Which question can be investigated by sampling each of four populations and gives numerical data for all four?
choices: What is the favorite color of each of the teens, young adults, adults and seniors in our town?
How many people live in our town, counting the teens, young adults, adults and seniors?
How many text messages per day do teens, young adults, adults and seniors in our town send?
Do the seniors in our town have phones, or do they prefer to use a landline at home?
questions.answer: How many text messages per day do teens, young adults, adults and seniors in our town send?
questions.solution: The question about text messages has four populations (the four age groups) and a number for each person. A favorite color is not a number, and the other questions concern one population or one answer.

solve.answer: How many text messages per day do teens, young adults, adults and seniors in our town send?
solve.work: Numerical data and four populations: texts per day by teens, young adults, adults, seniors. Favorite color is categorical; town population is one number; seniors only is one population and categorical.

questions.skill: Write a question that compares several populations
questions.stem: In the question "How do the numbers of siblings of students in grades 6, 7 and 8 compare?", what is the variable being measured and what separates the populations?
choices: The variable is the number of siblings, and the populations are the students in each grade
The variable is the grade, and the populations are the numbers of siblings that students have
The variable is the number of students, and the populations are the siblings in each grade
The variable is the school, and the population is all of the siblings of the students in the school
questions.answer: The variable is the number of siblings, and the populations are the students in each grade
questions.solution: Each student gives a number of siblings, which is the variable. The students are separated into populations by grade.

solve.answer: The variable is the number of siblings, and the populations are the students in each grade
solve.work: Measured variable: number of siblings; populations separated by grade.

questions.skill: Spot a biased or unclear survey question
questions.stem: Which survey question should be split into two separate questions?
choices: How many books do you check out of the library in each month of the school year, on average?
What time do you usually visit the library on a school day after your classes?
Which library service do you use most often, such as books, computers or study rooms?
Do you think the library should have longer hours and also have more computers for students?
questions.answer: Do you think the library should have longer hours and also have more computers for students?
questions.solution: A person may want longer hours but not more computers, so one answer cannot fit both ideas. The question should be split.

solve.answer: Do you think the library should have longer hours and also have more computers for students?
solve.work: 'Longer hours and also more computers' asks two things at once.

questions.skill: Spot a biased or unclear survey question
questions.stem: Students are asked, "How many hours do you sleep on a school night?" Which set of answer choices covers every possible answer with no overlaps?
choices: At least 0 and at most 6; at least 6 and at most 8; at least 8 and at most 10; at least 10 and at most 12
Less than 6; at least 6 and less than 8; at least 8 and less than 10; 10 or more
Less than 6; at least 6 and less than 8; at least 9 and less than 10; 11 or more
5 hours or less; exactly 6 or 7 hours; exactly 8 hours; exactly 9 or 10 hours
questions.answer: Less than 6; at least 6 and less than 8; at least 8 and less than 10; 10 or more
questions.solution: Good answer choices leave no gaps and have no overlaps. The set starting with "Less than 6" and ending with "10 or more" covers every number of hours exactly once. The set of ranges that begin and end at the same numbers overlaps at 6, 8 and 10. The other two sets leave out possible answers such as 8.5 hours, and the last also leaves out 5.5 hours and 12 hours.

solve.answer: Less than 6; at least 6 and less than 8; at least 8 and less than 10; 10 or more
solve.work: Option 1: <6, [6,8), [8,10), >=10 -- covers all nonnegative values, no overlap. Option 2 overlaps at 6,8,10 and misses >12. Option 3 has gaps (e.g. 5.5, 7.5). Option 4 misses [8,9) and [10,11).

questions.skill: Identify bias in how a sample is chosen
questions.stem: A researcher compares how many hours students at Schools A, B and C spend on homework. At School A she surveys students in the after-school homework club, at School B she surveys a random sample, and at School C she surveys students in the library. Why can't she fairly compare the three schools?
choices: She surveyed three schools instead of one, so the results cannot be compared with one another
Homework cannot be compared between schools, because every school gives its own kind of homework to students
She should have surveyed fewer students at School B, since a random sample must always be the smallest
The samples were chosen in different ways, so differences may come from how the students were picked
questions.answer: The samples were chosen in different ways, so differences may come from how the students were picked
questions.solution: Students in a homework club or in the library may do more homework than typical students, but the random sample is typical. A difference may reflect how the samples were chosen and not the schools themselves.

solve.answer: The samples were chosen in different ways, so differences may come from how the students were picked
solve.work: Different selection methods (homework club, random, library) introduce different biases, so differences may reflect sampling not schools.

questions.skill: Identify bias in how a sample is chosen
questions.stem: A school emails a survey about a new bus schedule to all 800 families. Only 12% reply. What is the biggest concern?
choices: Families with strong opinions are more likely to reply, so the replies may not represent everyone
A reply rate of 12% is too high, so the replies are too many to give a fair picture of the 800 families
Email surveys cannot reach families, so the school learned nothing from any of the replies
The school should have asked fewer families, because a survey of 800 families is too large
questions.answer: Families with strong opinions are more likely to reply, so the replies may not represent everyone
questions.solution: When few people reply, those who do are often the ones who feel strongly. Their answers may differ from the opinions of the families who did not reply.

solve.answer: Families with strong opinions are more likely to reply, so the replies may not represent everyone
solve.work: Low response rate -> nonresponse/voluntary bias: those with strong opinions more likely reply.

questions.skill: Identify bias in how a sample is chosen
questions.stem: A researcher compares grades 5, 6, 7 and 8 and takes the first 25 students from each grade who turn in a permission form. Why might this sample be biased?
choices: She sampled the same number of students from each grade, but a fair comparison needs different numbers
She sampled four grades instead of one, and a fair comparison must use only one grade at a time
Students who turn in forms first may differ from the other students in the grade
Permission forms are not allowed in surveys, so the students she asked cannot be counted
questions.answer: Students who turn in forms first may differ from the other students in the grade
questions.solution: The students who return forms first may be more organized or more interested than the rest, so they may not be typical of the grade. The sample was not chosen by chance.

solve.answer: Students who turn in forms first may differ from the other students in the grade
solve.work: First to turn in forms is a non-random group that may differ (more organised etc.).

questions.skill: Identify and carry out random sampling
questions.stem: Nia says, "My sample is random because I picked students from all four grades." Which response is best?
choices: She is right, because using students from all four grades always makes a sample random, whoever is picked
She is not yet right, because a sample is random only if the students in each grade were chosen by chance
She is wrong, because a random sample can never include students from every one of the grades
She is right, because the sample is large, and every large sample is a random sample
questions.answer: She is not yet right, because a sample is random only if the students in each grade were chosen by chance
questions.solution: What makes a sample random is that chance decides who is chosen. Including all four grades is useful, but Nia could still have picked her friends in each grade.

solve.answer: She is not yet right, because a sample is random only if the students in each grade were chosen by chance
solve.issues: Wording 'She is not yet right' is slightly odd; the key point holds.
solve.work: Including all grades does not make a sample random; random requires selection by chance. Option 1.

questions.skill: Design a simulation
questions.stem: A simulation of samples of 10 students from a school where 40% like soccer is run 20 times and then 200 times. Which statement is most likely true?
choices: The two estimates will be exactly the same, because they come from the same model
20 trials give a more exact answer than 200 trials, because there is less to average
The estimate of the chance from 200 trials is probably closer to the true chance
Running more trials changes what the model stands for, so the 200 trials model a different school
questions.answer: The estimate of the chance from 200 trials is probably closer to the true chance
questions.solution: More trials make the estimate settle closer to the true chance. The number of trials does not change the model, and two runs will usually not agree exactly.

solve.answer: The estimate of the chance from 200 trials is probably closer to the true chance
solve.work: More trials give a more stable estimate, probably closer to the true probability.

questions.skill: Estimate a probability from simulation results
questions.stem: A school has 50% pizza fans. In a simulation of 100 random samples of 10 students, 9 or 10 pizza fans happened in only 1 of the 100 samples. A real random sample of 10 students from another school has 9 pizza fans. What does this suggest?
choices: The other school probably has more than 50% pizza fans, since 9 of 10 is rare when the true percent is 50%
Exactly 90% of all of the students at the other school like pizza, since 9 out of the 10 students in the sample do
The real sample must be wrong because it differs from the simulation, so it should be taken again
Nothing can be learned from a random sample of 10, because a sample that small is always meaningless
questions.answer: The other school probably has more than 50% pizza fans, since 9 of 10 is rare when the true percent is 50%
questions.solution: In the simulation, a sample like this happened only about 1% of the time when the true percent is 50%. So it is likely that the other school has more than 50% pizza fans. A sample suggests a percent but does not prove an exact one.

solve.answer: The other school probably has more than 50% pizza fans, since 9 of 10 is rare when the true percent is 50%
solve.work: Under 50%, 9+ of 10 occurred 1/100 times (true P = 11/1024 ~ 1.1%), so 9 of 10 is unusual -> evidence the other school has more than 50% pizza fans.

questions.skill: Judge whether a sample is valid for several populations
questions.stem: Two researchers compare bike ownership at three schools with 200, 600 and 1,200 students. Researcher A takes a random sample of 20 students from each school. Researcher B takes a random sample of 60 students from each school. Which gives more reliable information for comparing the schools, and why?
choices: Researcher A, because fewer students are asked, so each of the answers can be checked closely
Neither, because the schools have different sizes, so the same sample size cannot be used
Neither, because a sample can never be used to compare schools, only asking everyone can
Researcher B, because larger random samples vary less from the true percents of each school
questions.answer: Researcher B, because larger random samples vary less from the true percents of each school
questions.solution: Larger random samples give percents that are closer to the true percents for each school. The school sizes do not make a smaller sample better.

solve.answer: Researcher B, because larger random samples vary less from the true percents of each school
solve.work: Larger random samples have less sampling variability: Researcher B (60 each).

questions.skill: Judge whether a sample is valid for several populations
questions.stem: Two random samples of 20 students each are taken at School A and School B. The sample from School A shows that 40% own a bike, and the sample from School B shows that 45% own a bike. Why shouldn't the researcher conclude that more students at School B own a bike?
choices: Samples should be taken from only one school, because two schools cannot be compared by sampling
Random samples are never reliable, because they are chosen by chance and not by the researcher
Random samples of 20 can differ by chance, so a difference of 5 percentage points may not be real
Bike percents cannot be compared between schools, because each school has different students
questions.answer: Random samples of 20 can differ by chance, so a difference of 5 percentage points may not be real
questions.solution: Small random samples vary from the true percent just by chance, so a 5-point difference could be due to chance. Larger samples would give a better comparison.

solve.answer: Random samples of 20 can differ by chance, so a difference of 5 percentage points may not be real
solve.work: With n=20, 40% vs 45% is 8 vs 9 students; sampling variability easily explains that. Option 4.

questions.skill: Compare the ranges of two data sets
questions.stem: Data set P is 3, 5, 5, 8, 9. Data set Q is 1, 4, 6, 7, 12. How much greater is the range of Q than the range of P?
questions.solution: The range of P is $9 - 3 = 6$. The range of Q is $12 - 1 = 11$. The difference is $11 - 6 = 5$.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of two data sets
questions.stem: Quiz scores for two classes are listed. Class A: 70, 75, 80, 85, 90. Class B: 60, 78, 82, 84, 96. Which statement is true?
choices: Class B's median is 2 points higher than Class A's median
Class A's median is 2 points higher than Class B's median
The two classes have the same median
Class B's median is 16 points higher than Class A's median
questions.answer: Class B's median is 2 points higher than Class A's median
questions.solution: The median is the middle value of the ordered list. Class A: 80. Class B: 82. So Class B's median is 2 points higher. (The two classes have the same mean, 80, but not the same median. The ranges are 20 and 36, which differ by 16.)

solve.answer: Class B's median is 2 points higher than Class A's median
solve.work: Median A = 80 (middle of 5). Median B = 82. B is 2 points higher.

questions.skill: Find the smallest range among three data sets
questions.stem: Three data sets are listed. Set X: 12, 15, 18, 20. Set Y: 10, 11, 13, 14. Set Z: 5, 9, 12, 21. What is the smallest range of the three sets?
questions.solution: Set X: $20 - 12 = 8$. Set Y: $14 - 10 = 4$. Set Z: $21 - 5 = 16$. The smallest range is 4.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Three gardens were checked on three days, and the number of tomatoes picked each day is listed. Garden X: 4, 6, 8. Garden Y: 5, 7, 9. Garden Z: 2, 5, 8. How much greater is the greatest of the three means than the least of the three means?
questions.solution: The means are 6 (Garden X), 7 (Garden Y) and 5 (Garden Z). The greatest is 7 and the least is 5, so the difference is $7 - 5 = 2$.

solve.work: Means: X = 18/3 = 6, Y = 21/3 = 7, Z = 15/3 = 5. Greatest minus least = 7 - 5 = 2.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four classes each asked five students how many pets they have. Class A: 0, 1, 2, 2, 3. Class B: 1, 1, 1, 4, 9. Class C: 2, 2, 3, 3, 4. Class D: 0, 0, 2, 6, 7. Which class has the greatest median number of pets?
questions.answer: Class C
questions.solution: Each list is already in order, so the median is the middle value: Class A has 2, Class B has 1, Class C has 3 and Class D has 2. The greatest median is 3, in Class C. (Class B has the greatest mean, but the question asks for the median.)

solve.answer: Class C
solve.work: Medians (middle of 5 sorted): A 2, B 1, C 3, D 2. Greatest is Class C.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Two sets of numbers are listed in the order they were collected. Set P: 8, 3, 9, 5, 7. Set Q: 11, 2, 13, 10, 6. How much greater is the median of Set Q than the median of Set P?
questions.solution: Put each set in order. Set P: 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, so its median is 7. Set Q: 2, 6, 10, 11, 13, so its median is 10. The difference is 3.

solve.work: P sorted 3, 5, 7, 8, 9: median 7. Q sorted 2, 6, 10, 11, 13: median 10. 10 - 7 = 3.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four data sets are listed. Which data set has a mean of 10?
questions.solution: The mean is the sum divided by the number of values. For 3, 5, 8, 14, 20 the sum is 50 and 50 divided by 5 is 10. The other sets have means 10.4, 9.8 and 12. (Three of the sets have a median of 10, but the question asks for the mean.)

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Three sets of numbers are listed. Set W: 5, 9, 14. Set X: 8, 10, 11, 12. Set Y: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. What is the greatest range of the three sets?
questions.solution: The ranges are $14 - 5 = 9$ for Set W, $12 - 8 = 4$ for Set X and $10 - 2 = 8$ for Set Y. The greatest is 9.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four teams each had three jumpers in a long-jump contest. The distances, in meters, are listed. Red team: 3.1, 3.4, 3.2. Blue team: 2.8, 3.9, 3.3. Green team: 3.0, 3.6, 3.1. Gold team: 2.9, 3.5, 3.0. Which team has the smallest range of distances?
questions.answer: Red team
questions.solution: Range is the greatest distance minus the least distance. Red: $3.4 - 3.1 = 0.3$. Blue: $3.9 - 2.8 = 1.1$. Green: $3.6 - 3.0 = 0.6$. Gold: $3.5 - 2.9 = 0.6$. The smallest range is 0.3, the Red team.

solve.answer: Red team

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Two bus routes were timed on five mornings. The trip times in minutes are listed. Route 1: 12, 18, 15, 20, 11. Route 2: 16, 17, 15, 18, 16. How many minutes greater is the range of Route 1 than the range of Route 2?
questions.solution: Route 1 has a range of $20 - 11 = 9$ minutes. Route 2 has a range of $18 - 15 = 3$ minutes. The difference is $9 - 3 = 6$ minutes.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Three sets all have a mean of 5. Set A: 5, 5, 5, 5. Set B: 3, 4, 6, 7. Set C: 1, 5, 5, 9. Which statement is true?
choices: Set A has a range of 5
Set B and Set C have the same range
Set C has the greatest range
Set B has the smallest range
questions.answer: Set C has the greatest range
questions.solution: The ranges are $5 - 5 = 0$ for Set A, $7 - 3 = 4$ for Set B and $9 - 1 = 8$ for Set C. Set C has the greatest range. Set A has the smallest range (its values are all the same), and Sets B and C do not have equal ranges.

solve.answer: Set C has the greatest range
solve.work: Ranges: A 0, B 7 - 3 = 4, C 9 - 1 = 8. Only 'Set C has the greatest range' is true (A's range is 0, B's is not smallest).

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: A quiz had scores from 1 to 5. The number of students at each score was: score 1, one student; score 2, three students; score 3, six students; score 4, three students; score 5, one student. Which best describes the shape of the data?
choices: Symmetric, with one peak in the middle
Skewed right, with a long tail toward high scores
Skewed left, with a long tail toward low scores
Two separate peaks with a gap between them
questions.answer: Symmetric, with one peak in the middle
questions.solution: The counts rise to a single peak at score 3 and fall away in the same way on both sides (1, 3, 6, 3, 1). The two halves match, so the shape is symmetric with one peak in the middle.

solve.answer: Symmetric, with one peak in the middle
solve.work: Counts 1, 3, 6, 3, 1: mirror image around score 3, single peak at 3: symmetric.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Four data sets are listed. Which one has two clusters with a large gap between them?
questions.solution: Look for a big jump between neighbouring values. In 1, 2, 2, 10, 11, 11, the values stay near 1 and 2, then jump to 10 and 11: two clusters with a gap of 7 between them. The other sets move up in steps of 1 or 0.

solve.work: 1, 2, 2 and 10, 11, 11 form two clusters with a gap from 2 to 10. Others are spread evenly.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three data sets are going to be plotted on one number line. Set A: 3, 8, 12. Set B: 5, 9, 15. Set C: 1, 7, 10. How far is it on the number line from the lowest value of all three sets to the highest value of all three sets?
questions.solution: The lowest value in any set is 1 (Set C) and the highest is 15 (Set B). The distance between them is $15 - 1 = 14$.

solve.work: Lowest of all is 1 (Set C), highest 15 (Set B). 15 - 1 = 14.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three sets will be plotted on one number line. Set A: 4, 9, 17. Set B: 12, 25, 31. Set C: 7, 22, 38. Which number line can show every value?
questions.answer: A line from 0 to 40
questions.solution: The lowest value is 4 and the highest is 38, so the line must start at 4 or lower and end at 38 or higher. Only the line from 0 to 40 does both. The line from 0 to 30 misses 31 and 38, the line from 5 to 35 misses 4 and 38, and the line from 10 to 40 misses 4, 7 and 9.

solve.answer: A line from 0 to 40
solve.work: Values run from 4 to 38. Only 0 to 40 contains both; 0-30 misses 31 and 38, 5-35 misses 4 and 38, 10-40 misses 4, 7, 9.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three data sets are shown as dot plots on the same number line, with one dot above a number each time that number occurs in a set. Set A: 2, 4, 4, 7. Set B: 4, 5, 7, 7, 9. Set C: 1, 4, 7. In all, how many dots are above the number 4?
questions.solution: Count the 4s in each set: Set A has two 4s, Set B has one and Set C has one. The total is $2 + 1 + 1 = 4$ dots.

solve.work: 4 appears twice in A, once in B, once in C: 4 dots.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three data sets are plotted on one number line. Two sets overlap when the stretch of line from the lowest to the highest value of one set shares some part with the other set's stretch. Set A: 2, 3, 5, 6. Set B: 5, 6, 7, 8. Set C: 11, 12, 12, 13. Which statement is true?
choices: Sets A and B overlap, and Set C is apart from both
No two of the sets overlap
questions.answer: Sets A and B overlap, and Set C is apart from both
questions.solution: Set A covers 2 to 6, Set B covers 5 to 8 and Set C covers 11 to 13. A and B share the stretch from 5 to 6, so they overlap. Set C starts at 11, after Set B ends at 8, so it overlaps neither of the others.

solve.answer: Sets A and B overlap, and Set C is apart from both
solve.work: A spans 2-6, B spans 5-8, C spans 11-13. A and B share 5-6; C touches neither.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display shows quiz scores. In it, a stem of 2 with a leaf of 1 means a score of 21. Stem 2 has the leaves 1, 4, 4 and 7. Stem 3 has the leaves 0, 4, 4, 4 and 9. The mode is the value that occurs most often. What is the mode?
questions.solution: Write out the scores: 21, 24, 24, 27, 30, 34, 34, 34, 39. The score 34 appears three times, more than any other score, so the mode is 34.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display shows the ages of people at a picnic. A stem of 1 with a leaf of 2 means 12 years old. Stem 1 has the leaves 2, 4, 7. Stem 2 has the leaves 0, 3, 3, 9. Stem 3 has the leaves 1, 5. How many of the people are 20 years old or older?
questions.solution: The ages are 12, 14, 17, 20, 23, 23, 29, 31, 35. The ages that are at least 20 are those on stems 2 and 3: 20, 23, 23, 29, 31, 35. That is 6 people.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display shows the weights, in pounds, of some puppies. A stem of 5 with a leaf of 1 means 51 pounds. Stem 5 has the leaves 1, 6. Stem 6 has the leaves 0, 3, 3, 8. Stem 7 has the leaves 2, 4. What is the range of the weights, in pounds?
questions.solution: The weights are 51, 56, 60, 63, 63, 68, 72, 74. The heaviest is 74 and the lightest is 51, so the range is $74 - 51 = 23$ pounds.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Two box plots are described by their minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Box plot A: 3, 7, 10, 14, 20. Box plot B: 5, 9, 12, 15, 18. Which statement is true?
choices: Box plot B has the greater median
Box plot A has the greater minimum
Box plot A has the smaller range
Box plot B has the longer box
questions.answer: Box plot B has the greater median
questions.solution: Medians: A is 10 and B is 12, so B has the greater median. Minimums: 3 and 5, so B has the greater minimum. Ranges: $20 - 3 = 17$ for A and $18 - 5 = 13$ for B, so A has the greater range. Boxes: $14 - 7 = 7$ for A and $15 - 9 = 6$ for B, so A has the longer box.

solve.answer: Box plot B has the greater median
solve.work: A: range 17, box 7, median 10, min 3. B: range 13, box 6, median 12, min 5. Only 'B has the greater median' is true.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: A histogram shows how many books 30 students read this summer. The bar for 0 to 2 books shows 4 students, the bar for 3 to 5 books shows 11 students, the bar for 6 to 8 books shows 9 students and the bar for 9 to 11 books shows 6 students. How many students read 6 or more books?
questions.solution: The students who read 6 or more books are in the last two bars: $9 + 6 = 15$ students.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: A school gives a prize to each class whose median score is at least 70. Class A: 65, 70, 80. Class B: 55, 60, 90. Class C: 70, 72, 74. Class D: 50, 75, 78. How many classes get a prize?
questions.solution: The medians are 70 (Class A), 60 (Class B), 72 (Class C) and 75 (Class D). Classes A, C and D have a median of at least 70, so 3 classes get a prize. (Class B has a very high score, but its median is only 60.)

solve.work: Medians: A 70 (yes), B 60 (no), C 72 (yes), D 75 (yes). 3 classes.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: The minutes that five customers waited were recorded at two cafes. Cafe 1: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. Cafe 2: 5, 5, 6, 7, 7. Which statement is true?
choices: Cafe 1 has the shorter mean wait
The waits at Cafe 2 vary more than the waits at Cafe 1
Every wait at Cafe 1 was longer than every wait at Cafe 2
The mean waits are equal, but the waits at Cafe 2 are more consistent
questions.answer: The mean waits are equal, but the waits at Cafe 2 are more consistent
questions.solution: Both cafes have a mean wait of 6 minutes. The waits at Cafe 1 range from 2 to 10 (range 8), while the waits at Cafe 2 range from 5 to 7 (range 2). So the means are equal, and Cafe 2 is more consistent.

solve.answer: The mean waits are equal, but the waits at Cafe 2 are more consistent
solve.work: Cafe 1 mean 30/5 = 6, range 8. Cafe 2 mean 30/5 = 6, range 2. Equal means, Cafe 2 more consistent.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Two sets are plotted on one number line. Set A: 5, 6, 6, 7, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9. Set B: 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 15. Which statement describes the shapes?
choices: Set A is roughly symmetric, and Set B is skewed right
Set A is skewed right, and Set B is roughly symmetric
Set A is skewed left, and Set B is skewed right
Set A is roughly symmetric, and Set B is skewed left
questions.answer: Set A is roughly symmetric, and Set B is skewed right
questions.solution: Set A is balanced around its middle value 7: the values 5, 6, 6 on the left match 8, 8, 9 on the right, so it is roughly symmetric. Set B has most of its values near the small end and a long tail stretching toward the large values 9 and 15, so it is skewed right.

solve.answer: Set A is roughly symmetric, and Set B is skewed right
solve.work: A is centred at 7 with matching sides: symmetric. B bunches at 1-4 with a long tail to 15: skewed right.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Two sets of ages are plotted on one number line. Set A: 11, 12, 12, 13. Set B: 11, 12, 12, 13, 40. How much greater is the range of Set B than the range of Set A?
questions.solution: The range of Set A is $13 - 11 = 2$. The range of Set B is $40 - 11 = 29$, because of the far-away value 40. The difference is $29 - 2 = 27$.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A is 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Set B is the same except that 12 is replaced by 60. Which of these is the same for both sets?
questions.answer: The median
questions.solution: Both sets have 10 as the middle value, so the median stays 10. The mean changes (from 10 to 19.6), the range changes (from 4 to 52) and the greatest value changes (from 12 to 60).

solve.answer: The median
solve.work: A: median 10, range 4, mean 10, max 12. B: 8,9,10,11,60 median 10, range 52, mean 19.6, max 60. Only median same.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A is 10, 10, 10, 10, and its mean is 10. Set B has those four values and one more value, 60. What is the mean of Set B?
questions.solution: The five values of Set B add up to $10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 60 = 100$. The mean is $100 \div 5 = 20$. The one far-away value 60 doubles the mean.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Two box plots are given as minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Plot A: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45. Plot B: 10, 20, 25, 30, 40. Which statement is true?
choices: Plot A has the greater median
Plot B has the greater range
Plot B has the greater IQR
Plot A has the greater IQR
questions.answer: Plot A has the greater IQR
questions.solution: The medians are both 25. The ranges are $45 - 5 = 40$ for A and $40 - 10 = 30$ for B, so A has the greater range. The IQRs are $35 - 15 = 20$ for A and $30 - 20 = 10$ for B, so A has the greater IQR.

solve.answer: Plot A has the greater IQR
solve.work: IQR A 35-15=20, B 30-20=10. Medians both 25. Range A 40, B 30. A has greater IQR.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Two box plots are drawn on one number line. Plot A has minimum 22 and maximum 71. Plot B has minimum 30 and maximum 65. How much greater is the range of Plot A than the range of Plot B?
questions.solution: The range of Plot A is $71 - 22 = 49$. The range of Plot B is $65 - 30 = 35$. The difference is $49 - 35 = 14$.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: Two histograms show the quiz scores of two classes. Class A: 60 to 69, 4 students; 70 to 79, 9 students; 80 to 89, 7 students; 90 to 99, 3 students. Class B: 60 to 69, 6 students; 70 to 79, 8 students; 80 to 89, 5 students; 90 to 99, 2 students. How many students in the two classes together scored 80 or above?
questions.solution: Class A has $7 + 3 = 10$ students at 80 or above. Class B has $5 + 2 = 7$. Together that is $10 + 7 = 17$ students.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: A histogram shows how many minutes 24 students spent on the bus. The bars show: 0 to 9 minutes, 3 students; 10 to 19 minutes, 9 students; 20 to 29 minutes, 6 students; 30 to 39 minutes, 4 students; 40 to 49 minutes, 2 students. Which best describes the shape of the data?
choices: Skewed left, with a tail toward the shorter times
Skewed right, with a tail toward the longer times
Symmetric, with the bars balanced around the middle
Uniform, with all of the bars about the same height
questions.answer: Skewed right, with a tail toward the longer times
questions.solution: The tallest bar (9 students) is near the short-time end, and the bars then get shorter and shorter toward the long times (6, 4, 2). A tail stretching toward the larger values means the data are skewed right.

solve.answer: Skewed right, with a tail toward the longer times
solve.work: Counts 3,9,6,4,2 (sum 24): peak at 10-19, tapering toward longer times: skewed right.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: Bakery A sold 12, 14, 15, 16 and 18 cakes on five days. Bakery B sold 20, 22, 23, 24 and 26 cakes on five other days. Which statement is supported by these data?
choices: Bakery A has the greater median number of cakes sold
Bakery A has the greater range of cakes sold
Every value for Bakery B is greater than every value for Bakery A
The values for the two bakeries overlap
questions.answer: Every value for Bakery B is greater than every value for Bakery A
questions.solution: The least value for Bakery B (20) is greater than the greatest value for Bakery A (18), so every B value is greater than every A value and the two sets do not overlap. Bakery B also has the greater median (23 against 15), and the two ranges are equal (6 and 6).

solve.answer: Every value for Bakery B is greater than every value for Bakery A
solve.work: A max 18 < B min 20, so every B value exceeds every A value. Medians 15 vs 23; ranges both 6; no overlap.

questions.skill: Compare distributions: outliers and medians
questions.stem: Test scores are listed for two groups. Group 1: 45, 82, 84, 85, 85, 86, 88. Group 2: 70, 75, 78, 80, 82, 85, 88. Which statement is true?
choices: Group 2 has an outlier, and its median is higher than Group 1's median
Neither group has an outlier, and the medians are equal
Group 1 has an outlier, and its median is lower than Group 2's median
Group 1 has an outlier, and its median is higher than Group 2's median
questions.answer: Group 1 has an outlier, and its median is higher than Group 2's median
questions.solution: Group 1 has one score, 45, far below all of the others, so it is an outlier. Group 2's scores are spread fairly evenly with no outlier. The median of Group 1 is the 4th of 7 values, 85. The median of Group 2 is 80. So Group 1 has an outlier and the higher median.

solve.answer: Group 1 has an outlier, and its median is higher than Group 2's median
solve.work: Group 1 median = 85; Q1 = 82, Q3 = 86, IQR 4, lower fence 76, so 45 is an outlier. Group 2 median = 80; Q1 = 75, Q3 = 85, IQR 10, fences 60 and 100, no outlier. Group 1 has an outlier and higher median.

questions.skill: Compare the means of two data sets
questions.stem: Data set A is 10, 12, 14, 16. Data set B is 9, 13, 19, 23. How much greater is the mean of B than the mean of A?

questions.skill: Compare the spread of three data sets with equal means
questions.stem: Three data sets each have six values and a mean of 10. Set A: 9, 9, 10, 10, 11, 11. Set B: 5, 8, 10, 10, 12, 15. Set C: 10, 10, 10, 10, 10, 10. Which set's values are the most spread out?
choices: They are equally spread out because their means are equal
questions.answer: Set B
questions.solution: Set A ranges from 9 to 11 (range 2). Set B ranges from 5 to 15 (range 10). Set C has no spread at all (range 0). Set B is the most spread out. Equal means do not mean equal spread.

solve.answer: Set B
solve.work: Range A = 2, B = 10, C = 0; B's values are farthest from 10.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Three sets of numbers are listed in the order they were collected. Set A: 14, 9, 16, 12, 19. Set B: 11, 20, 8, 13, 23. Set C: 10, 18, 15, 17, 5. What is the mean of the set that has the greatest median?
questions.solution: In order, Set A is 9, 12, 14, 16, 19 (median 14), Set B is 8, 11, 13, 20, 23 (median 13) and Set C is 5, 10, 15, 17, 18 (median 15). Set C has the greatest median. Its mean is $(10+18+15+17+5) \div 5 = 13$.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Set M is 3, 4, 4, 5, 24. Set N is 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Which statement is true?
choices: Set M has the greater mean
Set N has the greater median
Both sets have the same median
Set N has a mean that is different from its median
questions.answer: Set N has the greater median
questions.solution: Set M has a mean of 8 and a median of 4. Set N has a mean of 10 and a median of 10. So Set N has the greater median, and also the greater mean. The one very large value, 24, pulls the mean of Set M far above its median, but not past Set N's mean.

solve.answer: Set N has the greater median
solve.work: M: median 4, mean 40/5 = 8. N: median 10, mean 50/5 = 10. N has the greater median (true); N mean = median; medians differ; M mean 8 < 10.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four students each took four turns at a ring-toss game, and the points from each turn are listed. Mia: 12, 15, 9, 14. Noah: 13, 13, 12, 13. Owen: 7, 20, 10, 11. Pia: 16, 8, 14, 11. Which student has the greatest mean score?
questions.answer: Noah
questions.solution: The sums are Mia 50, Noah 51, Owen 48 and Pia 49. All four students took 4 turns, so the greatest sum gives the greatest mean. Noah's mean is 12.75. (Owen has the single highest score, 20, but not the highest mean.)

solve.answer: Noah
solve.work: Means: Mia 50/4 = 12.5, Noah 51/4 = 12.75, Owen 48/4 = 12, Pia 49/4 = 12.25. Noah greatest.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four data sets each have six values. Set 1: 3, 5, 8, 9, 12, 15. Set 2: 1, 4, 9, 12, 13, 20. Set 3: 6, 6, 7, 9, 9, 9. Set 4: 2, 3, 9, 10, 12, 12. What is the greatest of the four medians?
questions.solution: With six values, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values. Set 1: 8.5. Set 2: $(9 + 12) \div 2 = 10.5$. Set 3: 8. Set 4: 9.5. The greatest median is 10.5.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Sets A, B and C each have 8 values and the same range. Set A: 4, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 20. Set B: 4, 5, 6, 8, 12, 15, 18, 20. Set C: 4, 6, 8, 10, 14, 16, 18, 20. The IQR is Q3 minus Q1, using the medians of the lower four and upper four values. Which statement is true?
choices: Set B has the smallest IQR
Set C has the greatest IQR
The three sets have the same IQR because their ranges are equal
Set A has the smallest IQR
questions.answer: Set A has the smallest IQR
questions.solution: All three ranges are $20 - 4 = 16$. Set A: $Q_1 = 9.5$ and $Q_3 = 13.5$, so IQR $= 4$. Set B: $Q_1 = 5.5$ and $Q_3 = 16.5$, so IQR $= 11$. Set C: $Q_1 = 7$ and $Q_3 = 17$, so IQR $= 10$. Set A has the smallest IQR. Equal ranges do not mean equal IQRs.

solve.answer: Set A has the smallest IQR

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: The daily high temperatures, in degrees Fahrenheit, were recorded for five days in four towns. Town A: 61, 68, 70, 73, 65. Town B: 55, 57, 59, 56, 58. Town C: 48, 66, 52, 71, 60. Town D: 63, 64, 70, 66, 62. How much greater is the greatest range of the four towns than the smallest range?
questions.solution: The ranges are Town A $73 - 61 = 12$, Town B $59 - 55 = 4$, Town C $71 - 48 = 23$ and Town D $70 - 62 = 8$. The greatest is 23 and the smallest is 4, so the difference is $23 - 4 = 19$.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Two data sets are described by five numbers each: the minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum, in that order. Set A: 10, 20, 25, 30, 60. Set B: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45. Which statement is true?
choices: Set A has the greater range, and Set B has the greater IQR
Set A has the greater range and the greater IQR
Set B has the greater range and the greater IQR
Set B has the greater range, and Set A has the greater IQR
questions.answer: Set A has the greater range, and Set B has the greater IQR
questions.solution: Set A has a range of $60 - 10 = 50$ and an IQR of $30 - 20 = 10$. Set B has a range of $45 - 5 = 40$ and an IQR of $35 - 15 = 20$. Set A has the greater range, but Set B has the greater IQR.

solve.answer: Set A has the greater range, and Set B has the greater IQR
solve.work: A: range 60 - 10 = 50, IQR 30 - 20 = 10. B: range 45 - 5 = 40, IQR 35 - 15 = 20. A greater range, B greater IQR.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Eleven students counted the text messages they sent yesterday. The number of students in each group was: 0 to 10 messages, six students; 11 to 20 messages, three students; 21 to 30 messages, one student; 31 to 40 messages, one student. Which best describes the shape of the data?
choices: Symmetric, with one peak in the middle
Skewed left, with a long tail toward small numbers
Skewed right, with a long tail toward large numbers
Two separate peaks with a gap between them
questions.answer: Skewed right, with a long tail toward large numbers
questions.solution: Most of the students are in the lowest group, and the counts shrink steadily as the number of messages grows (6, 3, 1, 1). The tail stretches toward the large numbers, so the data are skewed right.

solve.answer: Skewed right, with a long tail toward large numbers
solve.work: Counts 6, 3, 1, 1 from low to high: peak at the low end, tail toward large numbers: skewed right.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Four data sets each have seven values. Which set is symmetric, with the values balanced evenly on both sides of the middle value?
questions.solution: In a symmetric set, the lowest and highest values are the same distance from the middle, and so are the next pair, and so on. For 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11 the middle value is 7 and the pairs 3 and 11, 5 and 9, 6 and 8 each add to 14. The other sets have a tail on one side, so they are not balanced.

solve.work: 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11: around 7 the distances are 4, 2, 1 below and 1, 2, 4 above: symmetric. Others have long tails one way.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A is 6, 7, 7, 8, 9. Set B is the same except that 9 is replaced by 40. By how much does the mean increase from Set A to Set B?
questions.solution: Set A has a mean of $6+7+7+8+9 = 37$ divided by 5, which is 7.4. Set B has a mean of 68 divided by 5, which is 13.6. The mean increases by $13.6 - 7.4 = 6.2$. (The median stays 7, but the mean changes.)

solve.work: A: sum 37, mean 7.4. B: sum 68, mean 13.6. Increase 6.2 (equivalently 31/5).

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Class P scores: 74, 76, 77, 78, 80. Class Q scores: 75, 77, 78, 79, 21. Which statement is true?
choices: The classes have the same median, but Class Q has the lower mean
Class Q has the lower median
Class P has the greater range
The classes have the same mean
questions.answer: The classes have the same median, but Class Q has the lower mean
questions.solution: Class P: median 77, mean 77, range 6. Class Q: median 77, mean 66, range 58. The medians match, but the one very low score, 21, pulls the mean of Class Q down.

solve.answer: The classes have the same median, but Class Q has the lower mean
solve.work: P: median 77, mean 385/5 = 77, range 6. Q sorted 21, 75, 77, 78, 79: median 77, mean 330/5 = 66, range 58. Same median, Q lower mean.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A is 40, 42, 43, 45, 46, 48. Set B is the same except that 48 is replaced by 120. Which statement is true?
choices: The median of Set B is much greater than the median of Set A
The medians are the same, but the range of Set B is much greater
questions.answer: The medians are the same, but the range of Set B is much greater
questions.solution: Both sets have a median of $(43 + 45) \div 2 = 44$, because the changed value is above the middle. The range jumps from $48 - 40 = 8$ to $120 - 40 = 80$, and the mean also rises (from 44 to 56).

solve.answer: The medians are the same, but the range of Set B is much greater
solve.work: Medians both (43+45)/2 = 44. Means 44 vs 56. Ranges 8 vs 80. Same medians, B's range much greater.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three sets are shown on one number line, with one dot for each value. Set A: 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5. Set B: 2, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6. Set C: 0, 0, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3. In all, how many dots are above numbers that are 3 or greater?
questions.solution: Count the values that are 3 or greater in each set: Set A has 6 (3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5), Set B has 9 (3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6) and Set C has 1 (3). The total is 16 dots.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three sets of lengths, in centimeters, will be plotted on one number line. Set A: 2.4, 3.1, 4.8. Set B: 1.9, 3.5, 5.2. Set C: 2.7, 4.0, 6.3. Which number line can show every value?
questions.answer: A line from 1 to 7
questions.solution: The lowest value is 1.9 and the highest is 6.3, so the line must start at 1.9 or lower and end at 6.3 or higher. Only the line from 1 to 7 works. The line from 2 to 6 misses 1.9 and 6.3, the line from 0 to 5 misses 5.2 and 6.3, and the line from 2 to 7 misses 1.9.

solve.answer: A line from 1 to 7
solve.work: Values run from 1.9 to 6.3. Only 1 to 7 contains both.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Set A and Set B are plotted on one number line. Set A: 2, 4, 6. Set B: 3, 5, 9, 11. What is the median of all the values shown on the line?
questions.solution: Put all seven values in order: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 11. The middle (4th) value is 5.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: The heights, in centimeters, of seedlings in three trays are plotted on one number line. Tray A: 40, 44, 45, 47, 52. Tray B: 42, 46, 50, 53, 60. Tray C: 38, 41, 43, 49, 55. Which statement is true?
choices: Tray C has the greatest range
Tray A has the greatest minimum
Tray B has the greatest median and the greatest maximum
Tray C has the greatest median
questions.answer: Tray B has the greatest median and the greatest maximum
questions.solution: Medians: Tray A 45, Tray B 50, Tray C 43. Maximums: 52, 60 and 55. Ranges: 12, 18 and 17. Minimums: 40, 42 and 38. Tray B has the greatest median and the greatest maximum; it also has the greatest range and minimum, so the other statements are false.

solve.answer: Tray B has the greatest median and the greatest maximum
solve.work: A: med 45, min 40, max 52, range 12. B: med 50, min 42, max 60, range 18. C: med 43, min 38, max 55, range 17. B has greatest median and max (true); C's range 17 < 18; B has greatest minimum.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A back-to-back stem-and-leaf display compares two sets of times, in seconds, using the same stems. A stem of 4 with a leaf of 1 means 41. Stem 4: Set A has the leaves 1, 3, 5 and Set B has 6, 8. Stem 5: Set A has 0, 2, 2, 6 and Set B has 1, 5, 7, 9. Stem 6: Set A has 1, 4 and Set B has 0, 2, 3, 3. How much greater is the median of Set B than the median of Set A?
questions.solution: Set A has 9 values: 41, 43, 45, 50, 52, 52, 56, 61, 64. Its median is the 5th value, 52. Set B has 10 values: 46, 48, 51, 55, 57, 59, 60, 62, 63, 63. Its median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values: $(57 + 59) \div 2 = 58$. The difference is $58 - 52 = 6$.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display shows the lengths of some fish, in inches. A stem of 2 with a leaf of 3 means 2.3 inches. Stem 2 has the leaves 3, 5, 7. Stem 3 has the leaves 0, 2, 2, 8. Stem 4 has the leaves 1, 6. What is the median length, in inches?
questions.solution: The lengths in order are 2.3, 2.5, 2.7, 3.0, 3.2, 3.2, 3.8, 4.1, 4.6. There are 9 values, so the median is the 5th one: 3.2 inches.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: Two sets are shown on a back-to-back stem-and-leaf display (a stem of 2 with a leaf of 1 means 21). Stem 2: Set P has the leaves 1, 5, 8 and Set R has 6, 9. Stem 3: P has 0, 2, 4, 4 and R has 5, 7, 8. Stem 4: P has 1, 3 and R has 0, 2, 2, 6, 9. Stem 5: P has none and R has 1, 5. Which statement is true?
choices: Set P has the greater median
Set P has the greater range
The two sets have the same number of values
Set R has the greater median, and Set P has the smaller range
questions.answer: Set R has the greater median, and Set P has the smaller range
questions.solution: Set P has 9 values: 21, 25, 28, 30, 32, 34, 34, 41, 43, with median 32 and range 22. Set R has 12 values: 26, 29, 35, 37, 38, 40, 42, 42, 46, 49, 51, 55, with median 41 and range 29. So Set R has the greater median, and Set P has the smaller range.

solve.answer: Set R has the greater median, and Set P has the smaller range

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Three box plots are described by their minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Plot X: 20, 35, 45, 60, 80. Plot Y: 30, 40, 50, 55, 70. Plot Z: 10, 30, 52, 65, 90. How much greater is the greatest IQR of the three plots than the least IQR?
questions.solution: The IQR is Q3 minus Q1. Plot X: $60 - 35 = 25$. Plot Y: $55 - 40 = 15$. Plot Z: $65 - 30 = 35$. The greatest is 35 and the least is 15, so the difference is 20.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: A box plot is drawn from these five numbers: minimum 10, Q1 28, median 30, Q3 36 and maximum 70. The whiskers run from the box to the minimum and to the maximum. Which statement is true?
choices: The median is exactly halfway between Q1 and Q3
Half of the values are greater than 36
The upper whisker is longer than the lower whisker
questions.answer: The upper whisker is longer than the lower whisker
questions.solution: The lower whisker is $28 - 10 = 18$ long and the upper whisker is $70 - 36 = 34$ long, so the upper whisker is longer. The halfway point between Q1 and Q3 is 32, not 30. Only a quarter of the values are above Q3 = 36. The IQR is $36 - 28 = 8$.

solve.answer: The upper whisker is longer than the lower whisker
solve.work: Lower whisker 28 - 10 = 18, upper 70 - 36 = 34: upper longer (true). IQR is 8, not 26. A quarter (not half) exceed 36. Halfway between 28 and 36 is 32, not 30.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: Two histograms show the scores of two classes. Class A: 90 to 100, five students; 80 to 89, nine students; 70 to 79, seven students; 60 to 69, four students. Class B: 90 to 100, three students; 80 to 89, six students; 70 to 79, eleven students; 60 to 69, five students. How many more students in Class A than in Class B scored 80 or above?
questions.solution: Class A: $5 + 9 = 14$ students scored 80 or above. Class B: $3 + 6 = 9$ students. The difference is $14 - 9 = 5$ students.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: Class A has 20 students, and 5 of them scored 90 or above. Class B has 40 students, and 8 of them scored 90 or above. Which statement is true?
choices: A greater percent of Class A than of Class B scored 90 or above
A greater percent of Class B than of Class A scored 90 or above, because more students in Class B did
The same percent of both classes scored 90 or above
Fewer students in Class B than in Class A scored 90 or above
questions.answer: A greater percent of Class A than of Class B scored 90 or above
questions.solution: Compare percents, not counts. Class A: $5 \div 20 = 25\%$. Class B: $8 \div 40 = 20\%$. A greater percent of Class A scored 90 or above, even though Class B has more such students (8 compared with 5).

solve.answer: A greater percent of Class A than of Class B scored 90 or above
solve.work: A: 5/20 = 25%. B: 8/40 = 20%. A greater percent. B has more students (8 > 5), so the last option is false.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: A coach timed three runners in five races. The times, in seconds, are listed. Runner A: 13, 11, 12, 14, 12. Runner B: 12, 10, 13, 11, 15. Runner C: 14, 13, 12, 12, 16. Of all 15 times, how many are faster (less) than the median time of Runner A?
questions.solution: Runner A's times in order are 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, so the median is 12. The times less than 12 are 11 (Runner A), 10 and 11 (Runner B), and none for Runner C. That is 3 times.

solve.work: A sorted 11, 12, 12, 13, 14: median 12. Times < 12: A: 11; B: 10, 11; C: none. Total 3.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: The prices of five homes in each of two neighborhoods are listed, in thousands of dollars. Neighborhood X: 220, 240, 250, 260, 900. Neighborhood Y: 280, 290, 300, 310, 320. Which statement is true?
choices: The median price is greater in Y, but the mean price is greater in X
Every home in X costs more than every home in Y
The mean price and the median price of X are equal
The prices in Y have the greater range
questions.answer: The median price is greater in Y, but the mean price is greater in X
questions.solution: Neighborhood X: median 250, mean 374, range 680. Neighborhood Y: median 300, mean 300, range 40. The one very expensive home (900) lifts the mean of X above that of Y, while the median shows that a typical home in Y costs more.

solve.answer: The median price is greater in Y, but the mean price is greater in X
solve.work: X: median 250, mean 1870/5 = 374, range 680. Y: median 300, mean 300, range 40. Median greater in Y, mean greater in X.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: Class P scores: 68, 72, 76, 78, 85. Class Q scores: 70, 79, 84, 88, 92. A score of 80 is compared with the median of each class. Which statement is true?
choices: The score of 80 is above both medians
The score of 80 is above the median of Class P and below the median of Class Q
The score of 80 is below both medians
The score of 80 is below the median of Class P and above the median of Class Q
questions.answer: The score of 80 is above the median of Class P and below the median of Class Q
questions.solution: The median of Class P is 76 and the median of Class Q is 84. A score of 80 is greater than 76 and less than 84, so it is above the median of Class P and below the median of Class Q.

solve.answer: The score of 80 is above the median of Class P and below the median of Class Q

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Sets A and B are plotted on one number line, and each has seven values. With seven values, Q1 is the median of the lowest three and Q3 is the median of the highest three (the middle value is left out). Set A: 12, 4, 9, 7, 15, 6, 10. Set B: 20, 8, 14, 3, 11, 17, 5. How much greater is the IQR of Set B than the IQR of Set A?
questions.solution: In order, Set A is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 15. Q1 is the median of 4, 6, 7, which is 6, and Q3 is the median of 10, 12, 15, which is 12. So its IQR is $12 - 6 = 6$. In order, Set B is 3, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20. Q1 is 5 and Q3 is 17, so its IQR is $17 - 5 = 12$. The difference is $12 - 6 = 6$.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Two sets are plotted on one number line. Set X: 3, 4, 4, 5, 6, 7, 25. Set Y: 1, 20, 21, 21, 22, 23, 24. Which statement is true?
choices: For both sets the mean is greater than the median
For Set X the mean is less than the median, and for Set Y the mean is greater than the median
For both sets the mean is less than the median
For Set X the mean is greater than the median, and for Set Y the mean is less than the median
questions.answer: For Set X the mean is greater than the median, and for Set Y the mean is less than the median
questions.solution: Set X has a median of 5. Its sum is 54, so its mean is about 7.7, pulled up by the large value 25. Set Y has a median of 21. Its sum is 132, so its mean is about 18.9, pulled down by the small value 1. So the mean of X is greater than its median and the mean of Y is less than its median.

solve.answer: For Set X the mean is greater than the median, and for Set Y the mean is less than the median
solve.work: X: median 5, mean 54/7=7.71 > median. Y: median 21, mean 132/7=18.86 < median.

questions.skill: Describe clusters and gaps in a distribution
questions.stem: Two sets are plotted on one number line. In each, the dots form two clusters. The gap is the empty stretch from the greatest value of the lower cluster to the least value of the upper cluster. Set A: 5, 6, 7, 8, 30, 31, 32. Set B: 5, 6, 7, 20, 21, 22. How much wider is the gap in Set A than the gap in Set B?
questions.solution: In Set A the lower cluster ends at 8 and the upper cluster starts at 30, so the gap is $30 - 8 = 22$. In Set B the lower cluster ends at 7 and the upper cluster starts at 20, so the gap is $20 - 7 = 13$. The gap in A is $22 - 13 = 9$ wider.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Two box plots are drawn on one number line. Plot A has minimum 12, Q1 30, median 40, Q3 52 and maximum 80. The box of Plot B is exactly as long as the box of Plot A, and the Q1 of Plot B is 41. What is Q3 for Plot B?
questions.solution: The box of Plot A runs from 30 to 52, so it is $52 - 30 = 22$ long. The box of Plot B is also 22 long and starts at 41, so it ends at $41 + 22 = 63$.

solve.work: Box A length 52-30=22; Q3 of B = 41+22=63.

questions.skill: Mean of two data sets combined
questions.stem: Group 1 has the values 3, 7 and 8. Group 2 has the values 5, 9, 11 and 13. What is the mean of all seven values together?
questions.solution: Add all seven values: $3 + 7 + 8 + 5 + 9 + 11 + 13 = 56$. Divide by 7: $56 \div 7 = 8$.

questions.skill: Compare interquartile ranges of four data sets
questions.stem: Four data sets are summarized by their minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile and maximum, in that order. Set A: 5, 12, 15, 20, 30. Set B: 3, 15, 18, 21, 45. Set C: 8, 10, 16, 22, 28. Set D: 14, 18, 21, 24, 26. Which set has the greatest interquartile range?
questions.answer: Set C
questions.solution: The interquartile range is the third quartile minus the first quartile. Set A: $20 - 12 = 8$. Set B: $21 - 15 = 6$. Set C: $22 - 10 = 12$. Set D: $24 - 18 = 6$. Set C has the greatest. (Set B has the greatest range, but that is a different measure.)

solve.answer: Set C

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display for 9 test scores is described here. Stem 6 has leaves 2 and 5. Stem 7 has leaves 0, 4, 4 and 8. Stem 8 has leaves 1, 3 and 9. (Stem 6 with leaf 2 means a score of 62.) What is the median score?
questions.solution: The scores in order are 62, 65, 70, 74, 74, 78, 81, 83, 89. There are 9 scores, so the median is the 5th one, which is 74.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: A quiz was given to three groups. Group P has 4 students with a mean score of 10. Group Q has 6 students with a mean score of 15. Group R has 10 students with a mean score of 12. What is the mean score of all 20 students together?
questions.solution: Each group's total is its size times its mean: $4 \times 10 = 40$, $6 \times 15 = 90$ and $10 \times 12 = 120$. The grand total is $40 + 90 + 120 = 250$. Divide by 20 students: $250 \div 20 = 12.5$.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Set H is 20, 22, 24, 26, 28. Set J starts as 17, 21, 25, 29, and a fifth value will be added so that Set J has the same mean as Set H. What must the fifth value be?
questions.solution: Set H has a mean of 24, so Set J needs a total of $5 \times 24 = 120$. The four values already there add to 92. The fifth value is $120 - 92 = 28$.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four data sets each have five values. Set P: 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Set Q: 2, 3, 6, 10, 14. Set R: 1, 8, 9, 9, 10. Set S: 1, 2, 3, 4, 25. Which set has the greatest difference between its mean and its median?
questions.answer: Set S
questions.solution: Mean and median for each set: P is 6 and 6 (difference 0). Q is 7 and 6 (difference 1). R is 7.4 and 9 (difference 1.6). S is 7 and 3 (difference 4). Set S has the greatest difference, because its one large value 25 pulls the mean up.

solve.answer: Set S
solve.work: P: mean 6, median 6, diff 0. Q: mean 35/5 = 7, median 6, diff 1. R: mean 37/5 = 7.4, median 9, diff 1.6. S: mean 35/5 = 7, median 3, diff 4. Set S.

questions.skill: Compare the centers (mean or median) of several data sets
questions.stem: Class P and Class Q each have 8 students. Class P has a mean score of 78 and a median score of 80. Class Q has a mean score of 82 and a median score of 76. Which statement must be true?
choices: The students in Class Q scored more points in total than the students in Class P
Every student in Class Q scored higher than every student in Class P
Class P has the greater mean
Class Q has the greater median
questions.answer: The students in Class Q scored more points in total than the students in Class P
questions.solution: The classes are the same size, so the class with the greater mean has the greater total: Class Q has $8 \times 82 = 656$ points and Class P has $8 \times 78 = 624$. The other statements fail: Class Q's median is lower (76 compared with 80), so Class Q has students at or below 76, while Class P has students at or above 80, so not every Class Q student scored higher; and Class P's mean is lower, not greater.

solve.answer: The students in Class Q scored more points in total than the students in Class P
solve.work: Same size (8): totals P = 624, Q = 656, so Q's total is greater (must be true). Q's median 76 < 80; 'every student' not implied; P's mean is smaller.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Set A has a smallest value of 13 and a range of 24. Set B has the same greatest value as Set A and a range of 15. What is the smallest value of Set B?
questions.solution: The greatest value of Set A is the smallest value plus the range: $13 + 24 = 37$. Set B has the same greatest value, 37, and a range of 15, so its smallest value is $37 - 15 = 22$.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Two sets each have 8 values. Set X: 2, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 30. Set Y: 5, 6, 8, 10, 14, 17, 19, 21. Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower four and upper four values. Which statement is true?
choices: Both the range and the IQR are greater for X
The range is greater for Y, but the IQR is greater for X
Both the range and the IQR are greater for Y
The range is greater for X, but the IQR is greater for Y
questions.answer: The range is greater for X, but the IQR is greater for Y
questions.solution: Set X: range $30 - 2 = 28$; $Q_1 = 8.5$ and $Q_3 = 12.5$, so IQR $= 4$. Set Y: range $21 - 5 = 16$; $Q_1 = 7$ and $Q_3 = 18$, so IQR $= 11$. X has the greater range (because of the single value 30), but Y has the greater IQR.

solve.answer: The range is greater for X, but the IQR is greater for Y
solve.work: X: range 28; Q1 (8+9)/2 = 8.5, Q3 (12+13)/2 = 12.5, IQR 4. Y: range 16; Q1 (6+8)/2 = 7, Q3 (17+19)/2 = 18, IQR 11. Range greater for X, IQR greater for Y.

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Two sets each have six values. Set A: 13, 21, 9, 17, 25, 11. Set B: 30, 18, 24, 12, 16, 22. With six values, Q1 is the median of the lowest three values and Q3 is the median of the highest three values. How much greater is the IQR of Set A than the IQR of Set B?
questions.solution: Set A in order is 9, 11, 13, 17, 21, 25: $Q_1 = 11$ and $Q_3 = 21$, so its IQR is $21 - 11 = 10$. Set B in order is 12, 16, 18, 22, 24, 30: $Q_1 = 16$ and $Q_3 = 24$, so its IQR is $24 - 16 = 8$. The difference is $10 - 8 = 2$. (Set B has the greater range, but Set A has the greater IQR.)

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Two classes of 28 students took a test. The number of students with scores in each interval is listed. Class 1: 50 to 59, two students; 60 to 69, six; 70 to 79, twelve; 80 to 89, six; 90 to 99, two. Class 2: 50 to 59, ten students; 60 to 69, three; 70 to 79, two; 80 to 89, three; 90 to 99, ten. Which statement is true?
choices: Class 1 is skewed right and Class 2 is symmetric
Both classes are symmetric about the same center, but Class 2 is much more spread out
Class 2 has a single peak in the 70s
Class 1 is more spread out than Class 2
questions.answer: Both classes are symmetric about the same center, but Class 2 is much more spread out
questions.solution: Class 1 counts (2, 6, 12, 6, 2) are balanced around the 70s with a single peak there. Class 2 counts (10, 3, 2, 3, 10) are also balanced around the 70s, but the peaks are at the two ends and the middle is nearly empty. So both are symmetric about the same center, and Class 2 is much more spread out.

solve.answer: Both classes are symmetric about the same center, but Class 2 is much more spread out
solve.work: Class 1: 2, 6, 12, 6, 2 (symmetric, one peak in 70s). Class 2: 10, 3, 2, 3, 10 (symmetric about the 70s, peaks at both ends, much more spread). Only the last statement is true.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three sets are plotted on one number line. Set A: 4, 8, 9, 15. Set B: 6, 7, 12. Set C: 3, 10, 11, 14, 20. What is the median of all the values shown?
questions.solution: There are 12 values in all. In order they are 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 20. The median is the mean of the 6th and 7th values: $(9 + 10) \div 2 = 9.5$.

questions.skill: Plot several data sets on one number line
questions.stem: Three sets are plotted on one number line. The values of Set A run from 14 to 38. The values of Set B run from 22 to 47. The values of Set C run from 30 to 62. For how many units of the number line do the stretches of all three sets overlap?
questions.solution: All three sets cover a part of the line only where the latest start and the earliest end meet. The latest start is 30 (Set C) and the earliest end is 38 (Set A). The shared stretch runs from 30 to 38, which is $38 - 30 = 8$ units.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: Three stem-and-leaf displays show test scores (a stem of 6 with a leaf of 4 means 64). Display A: stem 6 has leaves 1, 4, 8; stem 7 has 0, 2, 5, 5, 9; stem 8 has 3, 6. Display B: stem 6 has 5; stem 7 has 1, 3, 6, 8; stem 8 has 0, 2, 4, 7, 9; stem 9 has 1. Display C: stem 5 has 9; stem 6 has 2, 6, 6; stem 7 has 4, 5, 9; stem 8 has 1, 8.
