What is the range of the display that has the greatest median?
questions.solution: Medians: A has 10 values with median 73.5; B has 11 values (65, 71, 73, 76, 78, 80, 82, 84, 87, 89, 91) with median 80; C has 9 values with median 74. Display B has the greatest median. Its range is $91 - 65 = 26$.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display shows the populations of ten small towns, in thousands of people. A stem of 11 with a leaf of 2 means 11.2 thousand. Stem 11 has the leaves 2, 5. Stem 12 has the leaves 0, 4, 4, 9. Stem 13 has the leaves 1, 6, 8. Stem 14 has the leaf 3. What is the median population, in thousands?
questions.solution: The values in order are 11.2, 11.5, 12.0, 12.4, 12.4, 12.9, 13.1, 13.6, 13.8, 14.3. There are 10 values, so the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th: $(12.4 + 12.9) \div 2 = 12.65$ thousand.

questions.skill: Read a stem-and-leaf display
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf display of test scores splits each stem in two. A stem marked L holds leaves 0 to 4, and a stem marked H holds leaves 5 to 9, so 6L with leaf 3 means 63 and 6H with leaf 5 means 65. 6L: 1, 3. 6H: 5, 7, 9. 7L: 0, 2, 2, 4. 7H: 5, 5, 6, 8. 8L: 1, 3, 3. 8H: 6, 9. How many scores are from 75 to 84, including both 75 and 84?

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: Three box plots are described by their minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Plot X: 40, 52, 60, 68, 90. Plot Y: 55, 62, 70, 78, 85. Plot Z: 48, 58, 62, 66, 76. Which statement is true?
choices: Plots X and Y have the same IQR, but Plot X has the greater range
Plots Y and Z have the same IQR
Plot Z has the greatest range
Plot X has the smallest IQR
questions.answer: Plots X and Y have the same IQR, but Plot X has the greater range
questions.solution: IQRs: X $68 - 52 = 16$, Y $78 - 62 = 16$, Z $66 - 58 = 8$. Ranges: X $90 - 40 = 50$, Y $85 - 55 = 30$, Z $76 - 48 = 28$. X and Y have equal IQRs (16), and X has the greater range.

solve.answer: Plots X and Y have the same IQR, but Plot X has the greater range
solve.work: IQR: X 16, Y 16, Z 8. Range: X 50, Y 30, Z 28. X and Y same IQR, X greater range (true).

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: A box plot has a median of 50 and an IQR of 24. Q1 is 14 less than the median. What is Q3?
questions.solution: Q1 is $50 - 14 = 36$. The IQR is Q3 minus Q1, so Q3 is Q1 plus the IQR: $36 + 24 = 60$.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: A box plot has minimum 2, Q1 5, median 8, Q3 12 and maximum 20. Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower four and upper four values. Which set of eight values matches this box plot?
questions.solution: For 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 20: the minimum is 2 and the maximum is 20. The lower four are 2, 4, 6, 7, so $Q_1 = (4 + 6) \div 2 = 5$. The median is $(7 + 9) \div 2 = 8$. The upper four are 9, 11, 13, 20, so $Q_3 = (11 + 13) \div 2 = 12$. Each other set changes one value, which moves one of Q1 (to 4.5), the median (to 8.5) or Q3 (to 11.5).

solve.work: Need Q1 5, median 8, Q3 12. Option 1: median (8+9)/2 = 8.5, no. Option 2: Q1 (4+6)/2 = 5, median (7+9)/2 = 8, Q3 (11+13)/2 = 12, yes. Option 3: Q1 4.5, no. Option 4: Q3 11.5, no.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: A histogram of 50 values has five bars. Four of the bars show 6, 14, 8 and 2 values. The fifth bar is the tallest bar. What percent of all 50 values are in the tallest bar?
questions.solution: The four known bars hold $6 + 14 + 8 + 2 = 30$ values, so the fifth bar holds $50 - 30 = 20$ values. That is the tallest bar. As a percent of 50: $20 \div 50 \times 100 = 40\%$.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: A histogram shows the ages of 40 people at a concert. The bars show: 10 to 19 years, 11 people; 20 to 29 years, 6 people; 30 to 39 years, 5 people; 40 to 49 years, 9 people; 50 to 59 years, 6 people; 60 to 69 years, 3 people. In which interval does the median age fall?
questions.answer: 30 to 39 years
questions.solution: With 40 people, the median is the mean of the 20th and 21st ages when they are put in order. Add up the bars from the youngest: 11, then $11 + 6 = 17$, then $17 + 5 = 22$. The 20th and 21st people are both inside the third bar, so the median age falls in 30 to 39 years. (The tallest bar, 10 to 19 years, is not where the middle of the data is.)

solve.answer: 30 to 39 years
solve.work: 40 values: median between 20th and 21st. Cumulative: 11, 17, 22. Both the 20th and 21st fall in 30 to 39.

questions.skill: Read a histogram or frequency table
questions.stem: Three classes recorded how many students scored 90 or above. Class A: 10 of 40 students. Class B: 8 of 25 students. Class C: 12 of 60 students. What is the greatest of the three percents minus the least of the three percents?
questions.solution: Class A: $10 \div 40 = 25\%$. Class B: $8 \div 25 = 32\%$. Class C: $12 \div 60 = 20\%$. The greatest percent is 32 and the least is 20, so the difference is 12 percentage points.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: Set A: 38, 44, 49, 51, 53, 57, 61, 70. Set B: 41, 47, 50, 53, 55, 58, 60, 66. How many of the values in Set B are greater than the median of Set A?
questions.solution: Set A has 8 values, so its median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: $(51 + 53) \div 2 = 52$. The values in Set B that are greater than 52 are 53, 55, 58, 60 and 66. That is 5 values.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: Set A: 20, 22, 25, 27, 30. Set B: 28, 31, 35, 38, 40, 44. The two sets are plotted on one number line. Which statement is true?
choices: Every value in Set B is greater than every value in Set A
The median of Set A is greater than the median of Set B
More than half of Set B's values are greater than every value in Set A
The two sets do not overlap on the number line
questions.answer: More than half of Set B's values are greater than every value in Set A
questions.solution: The greatest value in Set A is 30. In Set B, five of the six values (31, 35, 38, 40, 44) are greater than 30, which is more than half. Not every value in B is greater than every value in A, because 28 is not. The sets do overlap (A reaches 30, and B starts at 28), and the median of A (25) is less than the median of B (36.5).

solve.answer: More than half of Set B's values are greater than every value in Set A
solve.work: A max 30, median 25; B median (35+38)/2 = 36.5, B min 28 < 30 so sets overlap. B values above 30: 31, 35, 38, 40, 44 = 5 of 6, more than half (true).

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: Set A has 4 values and a mean of 50. Set B has a mean of 62. When the two sets are put together, the mean of all the values is 58. How many values are in Set B?
questions.solution: Let Set B have $n$ values. The total of all the values is $4 \times 50 + 62n = 200 + 62n$, and there are $4 + n$ values with a mean of 58, so $200 + 62n = 58(4 + n) = 232 + 58n$. Then $4n = 32$ and $n = 8$. Check: $(200 + 496) \div 12 = 58$.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion by comparing groups in context
questions.stem: A teacher wants the class with a median score of at least 80 whose scores are the most consistent, meaning the smallest IQR. The classes have (median, IQR): Class A (82, 12), Class B (82, 6), Class C (79, 4), Class D (85, 18). Which class should the teacher choose?
questions.answer: Class B
questions.solution: First keep the classes with a median of at least 80: A, B and D. (Class C has the smallest IQR, but its median is only 79.) Among A, B and D the IQRs are 12, 6 and 18, so the smallest is 6, in Class B.

solve.answer: Class B
solve.work: Median at least 80: A (82), B (82), D (85); C (79) excluded. Smallest IQR among them: B (6).

questions.skill: Compare the spread (range or interquartile range) of several data sets
questions.stem: Four sets each have eight values. The IQR is Q3 minus Q1, where Q1 is the median of the lowest four values and Q3 is the median of the highest four. Set P: 2, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 40. Set Q: 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 24, 28, 30. Set R: 5, 10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 25. Set S: 6, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 22. Which set has the greatest range but the smallest IQR?
questions.answer: Set P
questions.solution: Ranges: P is $40 - 2 = 38$, Q is 20, R is 20, S is 16, so P has the greatest range. IQRs: P has Q1 = 18.5 and Q3 = 22.5, so IQR 4. Q has Q1 = 13 and Q3 = 26, so IQR 13. R has Q1 = 11 and Q3 = 21, so IQR 10. S has Q1 = 10 and Q3 = 18, so IQR 8. P also has the smallest IQR, so the answer is Set P. (One extreme value stretches the range of P but not its middle half.)

solve.answer: Set P
solve.work: P: range 38, Q1=(2+18... median of 2,18,19,20)=18.5, Q3=22.5, IQR 4. Q: range 20, IQR 26-13=13. R: range 20, IQR 21-11=10. S: range 16, IQR 18-10=8. P has greatest range and smallest IQR.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: The median of a box plot is closer to Q1 than to Q3 when the data are stretched out toward the larger values. Four box plots are given as minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Plot A: 10, 20, 24, 40, 70. Plot B: 12, 30, 45, 50, 60. Plot C: 5, 14, 20, 26, 35. Plot D: 0, 8, 12, 30, 52. For how many of the plots is the median closer to Q1 than to Q3?
questions.solution: Compare (median - Q1) with (Q3 - median). Plot A: 4 and 16, so closer to Q1. Plot B: 15 and 5, so closer to Q3. Plot C: 6 and 6, so equally far. Plot D: 4 and 18, so closer to Q1. Two plots (A and D) have the median closer to Q1.

solve.work: A: 24-20=4 vs 40-24=16 yes. B: 15 vs 5 no. C: 6 vs 6 equal, no. D: 4 vs 18 yes. Count 2.

questions.skill: Describe and compare the shapes of distributions
questions.stem: Sets X, Y and Z are plotted on one number line. Set X: 14, 15, 16, 17, 18. Set Y: 14, 15, 16, 17, 38. Set Z: 1, 15, 16, 17, 18. Which statement is true?
choices: All three medians are equal, and Set Y has the greatest mean and Set Z the least
All three medians are equal, and Set Y has the least mean and Set Z the greatest
Set Y has the greatest median and the greatest mean of the three sets
All three means are equal, because all three medians are equal
questions.answer: All three medians are equal, and Set Y has the greatest mean and Set Z the least
questions.solution: Each set has the middle value 16, so the medians are all 16. The means are 16 for Set X, $100 \div 5 = 20$ for Set Y (pulled up by 38) and $67 \div 5 = 13.4$ for Set Z (pulled down by 1). So Y has the greatest mean and Z the least.

solve.answer: All three medians are equal, and Set Y has the greatest mean and Set Z the least
solve.work: Medians all 16. Means: X 80/5=16, Y 100/5=20, Z 67/5=13.4. Y greatest, Z least.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: A value is an outlier if it is more than 1.5 times the IQR above Q3. Four sets are plotted on one number line, and the value 70 is one of the values in each. Set A: Q1 = 20, Q3 = 32. Set B: Q1 = 36, Q3 = 60. Set C: Q1 = 44, Q3 = 52. Set D: Q1 = 22, Q3 = 34. In how many of the four sets is 70 an outlier?
questions.solution: Upper fence = Q3 + 1.5 x IQR. Set A: IQR 12, fence $32 + 18 = 50$, and 70 is above it. Set B: IQR 24, fence $60 + 36 = 96$, and 70 is below it. Set C: IQR 8, fence $52 + 12 = 64$, and 70 is above it. Set D: IQR 12, fence $34 + 18 = 52$, and 70 is above it. So 70 is an outlier in 3 sets.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A has five values and a mean of 12. Set B has the same five values plus a sixth value, an outlier of 72. How much greater is the mean of Set B than the mean of Set A?
questions.solution: The five values of Set A add up to $5 \times 12 = 60$. Adding 72 gives a total of 132 for six values, so the mean of Set B is $132 \div 6 = 22$. The difference is $22 - 12 = 10$.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier when comparing data sets
questions.stem: Set A is 12, 14, 15, 17, 22. Set B is Set A with one more value, 100, added. Adding the 100 raises the mean by some amount and raises the median by some amount. How much greater is the rise in the mean than the rise in the median?
questions.solution: Set A: the sum is 80, so the mean is 16, and the median is 15. Set B has six values with a sum of 180, so its mean is 30, and its median is $(15 + 17) \div 2 = 16$. The mean rises by $30 - 16 = 14$ and the median rises by $16 - 15 = 1$. The mean rises $14 - 1 = 13$ more.

solve.work: A: mean 80/5=16, median 15. B: mean 180/6=30, median (15+17)/2=16. Mean rise 14, median rise 1, 14-1=13.

questions.skill: Read and compare box plots from five-number summaries
questions.stem: In a box plot, the lower whisker runs from the minimum to Q1, and the upper whisker runs from Q3 to the maximum. Four box plots are given as minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum. Plot W: 0, 10, 15, 22, 36. Plot X: 12, 20, 28, 40, 70. Plot Y: 5, 25, 33, 45, 60. Plot Z: 30, 36, 50, 62, 90. For how many plots is the upper whisker longer than the lower whisker?
questions.solution: Plot W: lower whisker $10 - 0 = 10$, upper $36 - 22 = 14$, so the upper is longer. Plot X: lower 8, upper 30, so the upper is longer. Plot Y: lower 20, upper 15, so the lower is longer. Plot Z: lower 6, upper 28, so the upper is longer. The upper whisker is longer for 3 plots.

solve.work: W: lower 10, upper 14 yes. X: lower 8, upper 30 yes. Y: lower 20, upper 15 no. Z: lower 6, upper 28 yes. Count 3.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: The variance of a data set is the mean of the squared distances of the values from the mean. The data set 3, 5, 7, 9 has a mean of 6. What is its variance?
questions.solution: The distances from the mean 6 are 3, 1, 1 and 3. Their squares are 9, 1, 1 and 9. The mean of the squares is $\frac{9+1+1+9}{4} = \frac{20}{4} = 5$.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation as spread
questions.stem: Two data sets have the same mean. Set X has a standard deviation of 2 and Set Y has a standard deviation of 7. Which statement is true?
choices: The values in Set Y are more spread out than the values in Set X
The values in Set X are more spread out than the values in Set Y
Both sets are equally spread out, because they have the same mean
Set Y has a greater mean than Set X
questions.answer: The values in Set Y are more spread out than the values in Set X
questions.solution: The standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean. A larger standard deviation means more spread. Set Y's is larger, so its values are more spread out.

solve.answer: The values in Set Y are more spread out than the values in Set X
solve.work: Larger standard deviation means more spread: Y (7) is more spread than X (2).

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: A data set has a variance of 25. What is its standard deviation?
questions.solution: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. $\sqrt{25} = 5$.

questions.skill: Find the mean and deviations from the mean
questions.stem: Five students counted the books they read this month: 3, 5, 6, 4 and 7. The first step toward a standard deviation is finding the mean. What is the mean number of books?
questions.solution: Add: 3 + 5 + 6 + 4 + 7 = 25. Divide by 5 values: 25 / 5 = 5.

questions.skill: Find the mean and deviations from the mean
questions.stem: The mean of a data set is 20. A deviation is a value minus the mean. What is the deviation of the value 14?
questions.solution: The deviation is 14 - 20 = -6. It is negative because 14 is below the mean.

questions.skill: Find the mean and deviations from the mean
questions.stem: A data set has a mean of 7 and contains the value 3. What is the square of the distance from 3 to the mean?
questions.solution: The distance from 3 to 7 is 4 (the deviation is -4). Squared: 4 x 4 = 16.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: A cashier served 4, 4, 4 and 8 customers in four 10-minute periods. The mean is 5. What is the variance of these counts? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Distances from 5: -1, -1, -1, 3. Squared: 1, 1, 1, 9. The sum is 12, and 12 / 4 = 3.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: A snail crawled 2, 2, 6 and 6 meters on four days. The mean is 4 meters. Find the variance of these distances. (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Each value is 2 away from 4, so each squared distance is 4. The mean of four 4s is 4.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: All five of Jo's quiz scores were 9. What is the variance of her scores?
questions.solution: Every score equals the mean, 9, so every distance from the mean is 0. The variance is 0.

solve.work: All values equal the mean 9, every deviation 0, variance 0.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: The squared distances of five values from their mean are 1, 4, 0, 4 and 1. What is the variance of the five values? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Add the squared distances: 1 + 4 + 0 + 4 + 1 = 10. Divide by 5 values: 10 / 5 = 2.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Two seedlings measure 2 cm and 8 cm. The mean height is 5 cm. What is the variance of the two heights? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Distances from 5 are -3 and 3. Squared: 9 and 9. The mean of 9 and 9 is 9. (3 is the standard deviation, 18 is the sum, 6 is the range.)

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Two bus trips took 3 hours and 7 hours. The mean is 5 hours. What is the standard deviation of the two trip times, in hours? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Distances from 5 are -2 and 2; squared they are 4 and 4. The variance is 4, and its square root is 2.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Two hiking trails are 1 mile and 9 miles long, with a mean length of 5 miles. Find the standard deviation of the two lengths, in miles. (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Distances from 5 are -4 and 4; squared they are 16 and 16. The variance is 16, and the square root of 16 is 4.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Four plants have 20, 20, 30 and 30 leaves. The mean is 25 leaves. What is the standard deviation of the leaf counts? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Every value is 5 from the mean, so every squared distance is 25. The variance is 25, so the standard deviation is 5.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: The temperatures at dawn on two days were -3 and 3 degrees, so the mean is 0 degrees. What is the standard deviation of the two temperatures? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: Distances from 0 are 3 and 3; squared they are 9 and 9. The variance is 9, so the standard deviation is 3. (9 is the variance, 6 is the range, 0 is the mean.)

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: A data set has a standard deviation of 9. What is its variance?
questions.solution: The variance is the standard deviation squared: 9 x 9 = 81.

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: Which statement correctly relates the variance and the standard deviation of a data set?
choices: The standard deviation is the square of the variance
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance
The standard deviation is half of the variance
The variance is the square root of the standard deviation
questions.answer: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance
questions.solution: Squaring the standard deviation gives the variance, so taking the square root of the variance gives the standard deviation.

solve.answer: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: A calculator reports a variance of 144 for a list of race times. What is the standard deviation of the times?
questions.solution: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. The square root of 144 is 12, because 12 x 12 = 144.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: Class A and Class B both have a mean test score of 80. Class A's scores run from 78 to 82. Class B's scores run from 60 to 100. Which class most likely has the larger standard deviation?
choices: Class A, since its scores are closer to the mean
Class B, since its scores are more spread out
Class A, since its scores are all about equal
Neither, since the two means are the same
questions.answer: Class B, since its scores are more spread out
questions.solution: The standard deviation measures spread around the mean. Class B's scores are much more spread out, so its standard deviation is larger.

solve.answer: Class B, since its scores are more spread out
solve.work: Same mean; B spans 60-100 vs A 78-82, so B is more spread out and most likely has the larger SD.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: Each list has a mean of 5. Which list has the smallest standard deviation?
questions.solution: The list 5, 5, 5, 5 has no spread at all: every value is the mean, so its standard deviation is 0. The others are spread out by different amounts.

solve.work: 5,5,5,5 has SD 0, the smallest possible; others are positive.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: What does a larger standard deviation tell you about a data set?
choices: The values are more spread out from the mean
The mean of the values is larger
The data set has more values in it
The values are all larger numbers
questions.answer: The values are more spread out from the mean
questions.solution: Standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean. A larger one means more spread, not a larger mean or more values.

solve.answer: The values are more spread out from the mean
solve.work: Larger SD means values lie farther from the mean on average.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: A data set has a standard deviation of 0. What must be true?
choices: The mean of the values is 0
All the values are the same
questions.answer: All the values are the same
questions.solution: A standard deviation of 0 means no value is any distance from the mean, so every value equals the mean.

solve.answer: All the values are the same
solve.work: SD 0 means every squared distance is 0, so every value equals the mean: all the same.

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: Mr. Ray adds 8 points to every score on a quiz. What happens to the standard deviation of the scores?
questions.answer: It stays the same
questions.solution: Adding the same number to every value slides the whole data set up. The distances between values do not change, so the spread stays the same.

solve.answer: It stays the same
solve.work: Adding a constant shifts every value and the mean equally; deviations unchanged, SD unchanged.

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: Every plant in a garden grows exactly 10 centimeters taller. Before the growth, the mean height was 25 centimeters. What is the mean height afterward, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Adding 10 to every height adds 10 to the mean: 25 + 10 = 35.

solve.work: Adding 10 to every value adds 10 to the mean: 25 + 10 = 35.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Which statement best describes an outlier in a data set?
choices: A value far away from most of the other values
The value that appears most often
The value exactly in the middle
The value equal to the mean
questions.answer: A value far away from most of the other values
questions.solution: An outlier is an unusually large or small value that sits far from the rest of the data.

solve.answer: A value far away from most of the other values
solve.work: An outlier lies far from most of the other values.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Which value in this list is the outlier? Give that value. 12, 14, 13, 15, 14, 60
questions.solution: Most values are between 12 and 15. The value 60 is far from all of them, so it is the outlier.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: A data set has a standard deviation of 3. A new, extremely large value is added, far above all the others. What most likely happens to the standard deviation?
questions.answer: It gets larger
questions.solution: The new value is far from the mean, so its squared distance is very large. That makes the mean squared distance, and so the standard deviation, larger.

solve.answer: It gets larger
solve.work: A value far from the mean adds a large squared distance; SD grows.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: Which of these is a measure of spread?
questions.answer: Range
questions.solution: The mean, median and mode describe the centre of a data set. The range, the largest minus the smallest value, describes spread.

solve.answer: Range
solve.work: Mode, mean, median are centre; range is spread.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: Which pair has one measure of centre and one measure of spread?
questions.answer: Median and standard deviation
questions.solution: The median is a measure of centre and the standard deviation is a measure of spread. The other pairs are two centres or two spreads.

solve.answer: Median and standard deviation
solve.work: Median (centre) + SD (spread). Others: two centres, two centres, two spreads.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: A set of test scores has a mean of 40 and a standard deviation of 5. How many standard deviations above the mean is a score of 50?
questions.solution: The score is 50 - 40 = 10 points above the mean. One standard deviation is 5 points, so 10 / 5 = 2.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: Heights in a class have a mean of 100 centimeters and a standard deviation of 10 centimeters. What height is exactly 1 standard deviation below the mean?
questions.answer: 90 centimeters
questions.solution: One standard deviation below the mean is 100 - 10 = 90 centimeters.

solve.answer: 90 centimeters

questions.skill: Compare distributions by centre and spread
questions.stem: Two bakeries both have a mean wait of 5 minutes. Bakery P has a standard deviation of 1 minute and Bakery Q has a standard deviation of 3 minutes. Which has the more consistent wait?
choices: Bakery P, because its waits vary less
Bakery Q, because its waits vary more
Both, because the means are equal
Bakery Q, because its standard deviation is larger
questions.answer: Bakery P, because its waits vary less
questions.solution: The smaller the standard deviation, the less the waits vary, so Bakery P is more consistent.

solve.answer: Bakery P, because its waits vary less
solve.work: Smaller SD = more consistent: P (1 min).

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: A set of 6 bike-ride lengths has squared distances from the mean that add up to 150. What is the standard deviation of the ride lengths? (The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of the squared distances from the mean: divide by the number of values.)
questions.solution: The mean of the squared distances is 150 / 6 = 25. The standard deviation is the square root of 25, which is 5.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: The data set 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9 has a mean of 5. What is its standard deviation? (The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The distances from 5 are 3, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 2 and 4. Their squares are 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4 and 16, which add up to 32. The mean of the squares is $32 \div 8 = 4$. The standard deviation is $\sqrt{4} = 2$.

questions.skill: Effect of adding a constant on center and spread
questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 10. What happens to the mean and to the standard deviation of the data set?
choices: The mean and the standard deviation both go up by 10
The mean goes up by 10 and the standard deviation stays the same
The mean stays the same and the standard deviation goes up by 10
The mean goes up by 10 and the standard deviation is multiplied by 10
questions.answer: The mean goes up by 10 and the standard deviation stays the same
questions.solution: Adding 10 to every value slides the whole data set up by 10, so the mean goes up by 10. The distances between the values and the mean do not change, so the standard deviation stays the same.

solve.answer: The mean goes up by 10 and the standard deviation stays the same
solve.work: Adding 10 shifts every value and the mean by 10; distances from the mean are unchanged, so SD stays the same.

questions.skill: Compare standard deviations without computing
questions.stem: Three data sets each have five values and a mean of 10. Set 1: 9, 10, 10, 10, 11. Set 2: 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Set 3: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Which set has the greatest standard deviation?
choices: All three have the same standard deviation, because the means are equal
questions.answer: Set 3
questions.solution: The standard deviation is larger when values are farther from the mean. Set 3's values are the farthest from 10, and Set 1's are the closest. Equal means do not mean equal standard deviations.

solve.answer: Set 3
solve.work: Set 3 has values farthest from 10 (deviations 10, 5, 0, 5, 10) versus Set 2 (4, 2, 0, 2, 4) and Set 1 (1, 0, 0, 0, 1). Set 3 greatest SD.

questions.skill: Find the mean and deviations from the mean
questions.stem: For any data set, the signed deviations are each value minus the mean. What is the sum of all the signed deviations?
choices: It is always the number of values
questions.answer: It is always 0
questions.solution: The values above the mean and the values below the mean balance exactly, so the signed deviations always add to 0.

solve.answer: It is always 0

questions.skill: Find the mean and deviations from the mean
questions.stem: A data set of 4 values has a mean of 10. Three of the values are 3, 5 and 4 away from the mean, with deviations of -3, 5 and -4. What is the deviation of the fourth value?
questions.solution: The four deviations must add to 0. The three known ones add to -3 + 5 - 4 = -2, so the fourth deviation is 2.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Ana ran four sprints in 2, 6, 6 and 10 seconds. What is the variance of her times? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 24 / 4 = 6. Distances: -4, 0, 0, 4. Squared: 16, 0, 0, 16. The sum is 32, and 32 / 4 = 8.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: A team scored 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 goals in five games. Find the variance of the goals. (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 15 / 5 = 3. Distances: -2, -1, 0, 1, 2. Squared: 4, 1, 0, 1, 4. The sum is 10, and 10 / 5 = 2.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Four friends have 3, 3, 5 and 9 stickers. What is the variance of their sticker counts? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 20 / 4 = 5. Squared distances: 4, 4, 0, 16. The sum is 24, and 24 / 4 = 6. (24 is the sum of the squares, 4.8 divides by 5 instead of 4, and 5 is the mean.)

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: A shop counted 2, 2, 4, 8, 10 and 10 customers in six different hours. What is the variance of these counts? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 36 / 6 = 6. Distances: -4, -4, -2, 2, 4, 4. Squared: 16, 16, 4, 4, 16, 16. The sum is 72, and 72 / 6 = 12.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Three chapters have 3, 5 and 10 pages, with a mean of 6 pages. Which expression gives the variance of the page counts?
questions.solution: The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean: square each value minus 6, add, and divide by the 3 values. The others use the values themselves, skip the squaring, or divide by the wrong number.

solve.work: Variance = mean of squared deviations: sum of (x-6)^2 divided by n = 3.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: The ages of four neighbors are 3, 9, 11 and 17 years. Find the standard deviation of their ages, in years. (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 40 / 4 = 10. Distances: -7, -1, 1, 7. Squared: 49, 1, 1, 49. The sum is 100, and 100 / 4 = 25. The square root of 25 is 5.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Five boxes weigh 7, 9, 10, 11 and 13 kilograms. What is the standard deviation of the weights, in kilograms? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 50 / 5 = 10. Squared distances: 9, 1, 0, 1, 9. The sum is 20, and 20 / 5 = 4, the variance. The standard deviation is the square root of 4, which is 2.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Six shelves hold 14, 14, 14, 20, 20 and 20 books. Find the standard deviation of the number of books per shelf. (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 102 / 6 = 17. Each value is 3 from the mean, so each squared distance is 9. The variance is 9, and the standard deviation is 3.

solve.work: Mean 102/6 = 17; every deviation +-3, squares 9; variance 9; SD 3.

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: Data set P has a variance of 81 and data set Q has a variance of 64. How much greater is the standard deviation of P than the standard deviation of Q?
questions.solution: The standard deviation of P is the square root of 81, which is 9. For Q it is the square root of 64, which is 8. The difference is 9 - 8 = 1.

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: The standard deviation of a set of waiting times is 1.5 minutes. What is the variance of the waiting times, in square minutes?
questions.solution: The variance is the square of the standard deviation: 1.5 x 1.5 = 2.25.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: Lists A, B and C each have a mean of 20. A: 20, 20, 20, 20. B: 18, 19, 21, 22. C: 10, 15, 25, 30. Which choice puts the lists in order from smallest to largest standard deviation?
questions.answer: A, B, C
questions.solution: List A has no spread. List B stays within 2 of the mean. List C reaches 10 from the mean. So the order is A, B, C.

solve.answer: A, B, C
solve.work: A: SD 0. B: squares 4,1,1,4 -> var 2.5. C: squares 100,25,25,100 -> var 62.5. Order A, B, C.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: Set P is 0, 5, 5, 5, 10 and set Q is 0, 0, 5, 10, 10. Both have a mean of 5 and a range of 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Set P has the greater standard deviation, since more of its values equal the mean
Set Q has the greater standard deviation, since more values are far from the mean
The standard deviations are equal, since the means and ranges are equal
Set P has the greater standard deviation, since its middle values are all the same
questions.answer: Set Q has the greater standard deviation, since more values are far from the mean
questions.solution: In Q, four of the five values are 5 away from the mean. In P only two are. Q's squared distances are larger on average, so its variance (20 against 10) and standard deviation are greater.

solve.answer: Set Q has the greater standard deviation, since more values are far from the mean

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: The songs on an album have lengths with a standard deviation of 2 minutes. Each length is changed from minutes to seconds. What is the standard deviation of the lengths in seconds?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 60 multiplies the standard deviation by 60: 2 x 60 = 120 seconds.

solve.work: Multiplying every value by 60 multiplies SD by 60: 120.

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: Ms. Lee adds 5 bonus points to every student's score. Before the bonus, the mean was 72 and the standard deviation was 8. What is the mean after the bonus?
questions.solution: Adding 5 to every score adds 5 to the mean: 72 + 5 = 77. (The standard deviation stays 8.)

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: A rope company doubles the length of every rope it sells. The old lengths had a mean of 14 feet and a standard deviation of 3 feet. What is the standard deviation of the new lengths, in feet?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 2 multiplies the standard deviation by 2: 3 x 2 = 6.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Five friends used 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 gigabytes of data in a month. A sixth friend, who streams a lot, used 52 gigabytes. What is the mean for all six friends, in gigabytes?
questions.solution: The total is 8 + 9 + 10 + 11 + 12 + 52 = 102. Dividing by 6 gives 17. The one large value pulls the mean far above the first five.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: One extremely large outlier is added to a data set. Which statement is most likely true?
choices: The median changes a lot more than the mean does
The mean and the median both stay exactly the same
The mean and the median change by the same amount
The mean changes a lot more than the median does
questions.answer: The mean changes a lot more than the median does
questions.solution: The mean uses the size of every value, so an extreme value drags it. The median depends only on the order of the values, so it moves little.

solve.answer: The mean changes a lot more than the median does
solve.work: The mean is pulled toward the outlier; the median moves at most one position.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Sam was absent for a quiz and got 0. His class's other scores were 72, 76, 78 and 74. What is the mean of those four scores, with the 0 left out?
questions.solution: The four scores add to 72 + 76 + 78 + 74 = 300. Dividing by 4 gives 75.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: A club's members are 14, 15, 15, 17, 18 and 71 years old. The 71-year-old is the coach. By how much does the range of the ages decrease if the coach is left out?
questions.solution: With the coach the range is 71 - 14 = 57. Without the coach it is 18 - 14 = 4. The range decreases by 57 - 4 = 53.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: House prices in a town are mostly between 150 and 250 thousand dollars, but a few mansions cost over 2 million dollars. Which measure best describes how much typical prices vary?
choices: The IQR, since extreme prices hardly affect it
The range, since it shows the mansions too
The standard deviation, since it uses every price
The variance, since it squares the distances
questions.answer: The IQR, since extreme prices hardly affect it
questions.solution: A few extreme prices stretch the range, the variance and the standard deviation. The IQR uses only the middle half of the prices, so it describes typical variation.

solve.answer: The IQR, since extreme prices hardly affect it
solve.work: Extreme mansions distort range, variance and SD; IQR is resistant.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: A coach wants a measure of spread that uses every value in the data set. Which should she choose?
questions.answer: The standard deviation
questions.solution: The range uses only the smallest and largest values and the IQR uses only the quartiles. The median is a measure of centre. The standard deviation uses every value.

solve.answer: The standard deviation
solve.work: Range uses 2 values, IQR quartiles, median is centre; SD uses every value.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: Why is the IQR called a resistant measure of spread?
choices: It uses every value in the data, so extremes are simply averaged out
It is always larger than the standard deviation for the same data
It uses only the middle half of the values, so extremes hardly matter
It is always equal to the range when the data are symmetric
questions.answer: It uses only the middle half of the values, so extremes hardly matter
questions.solution: The IQR is the distance between the quartiles, so it ignores the lowest quarter and the highest quarter of the data, where outliers sit.

solve.answer: It uses only the middle half of the values, so extremes hardly matter
solve.work: IQR = Q3 - Q1, based on the middle half, so extremes hardly affect it.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: A set of times has a mean of 20 minutes and a standard deviation of 3 minutes. Which time is within 1 standard deviation of the mean?
questions.answer: 22 minutes
questions.solution: Within 1 standard deviation means between 20 - 3 = 17 and 20 + 3 = 23 minutes. Only 22 is in that range.

solve.answer: 22 minutes
solve.work: Within 1 SD: 17 to 23. Only 22 fits (15, 26, 29 outside).

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: A set of scores has a mean of 64 and a standard deviation of 6. A score of 79 is how many standard deviations above the mean?
questions.solution: The score is 79 - 64 = 15 points above the mean. Each standard deviation is 6 points, so 15 / 6 = 2.5.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: Scores on an exam have a mean of 500 and a standard deviation of 40. What score is 2.5 standard deviations above the mean?
questions.solution: 2.5 standard deviations is 2.5 x 40 = 100 points. Add to the mean: 500 + 100 = 600.

questions.skill: Compare distributions by centre and spread
questions.stem: Route A has a mean trip time of 20 minutes and a standard deviation of 2 minutes. Route B has a mean of 18 minutes and a standard deviation of 7 minutes. Which statement is true?
choices: Route A is faster on average and more predictable
Route B is faster on average but less predictable
Route B is faster on average and more predictable
Route A is slower on average and less predictable
questions.answer: Route B is faster on average but less predictable
questions.solution: Route B has the smaller mean, so it is faster on average. Route B has the larger standard deviation, so its times vary more and are less predictable.

solve.answer: Route B is faster on average but less predictable
solve.work: B mean 18 < 20 (faster), SD 7 > 2 (less predictable). A is slower but more predictable, so other options false.

questions.skill: Use technology output for spread
questions.stem: A student enters six test scores into a calculator. It shows a mean of 84 and a standard deviation of 0. What does this tell you?
questions.answer: All six scores are 84
questions.solution: A standard deviation of 0 means no score differs from the mean, so every score equals the mean, 84.

solve.answer: All six scores are 84
solve.work: SD 0 means all values equal the mean, 84.

questions.skill: Use technology output for spread
questions.stem: A spreadsheet reports that the squared distances from the mean of 12 test scores add up to 300. The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean (divide by the number of scores, 12). What is the variance of the 12 scores?
questions.solution: Variance = (sum of squared distances) / (number of values) = 300 / 12 = 25.

questions.skill: Compare standard deviations of two data sets
questions.stem: Data set X is 6, 6, 14, 14. Data set Y is 8, 8, 12, 12. Both sets have a mean of 10. How much greater is the standard deviation of X than the standard deviation of Y?
questions.solution: In X, every value is 4 away from the mean, so every squared distance is 16, the variance is 16 and the standard deviation is 4. In Y, every value is 2 away, so every squared distance is 4, the variance is 4 and the standard deviation is 2. The difference is $4 - 2 = 2$.

solve.work: X: every value is 4 from 10, so SD = 4. Y: every value is 2 from 10, so SD = 2. Difference = 2.

questions.skill: Use the mean and standard deviation to compare two scores
questions.stem: On a test, the mean score is 70 and the standard deviation is 5. Mia's score is 2 standard deviations above the mean. Leo's score is 1.5 standard deviations below the mean. How many points higher is Mia's score than Leo's score?
questions.solution: Mia's score is $70 + 2 \times 5 = 80$. Leo's score is $70 - 1.5 \times 5 = 62.5$. The difference is $80 - 62.5 = 17.5$ points.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread when there are outliers
questions.stem: A data set has a few extremely large values that are far from the rest of the data. Which measure of spread is least affected by those extreme values?
questions.answer: The interquartile range
questions.solution: The range, the variance and the standard deviation all use the extreme values, so a few very large values change them a lot. The interquartile range uses only the middle half of the data, so it is hardly affected.

solve.answer: The interquartile range
solve.work: The IQR uses only the middle 50% of the data, so extreme values barely affect it; range, variance and SD all use the extremes.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Four numbers are 4, 8, 8 and x. Their mean is 7. What is the variance of the four numbers? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The sum is 4 x 7 = 28, so x = 28 - 4 - 8 - 8 = 8. Distances from 7: -3, 1, 1, 1. Squared: 9, 1, 1, 1. The sum is 12, and 12 / 4 = 3.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: Five weekly savings amounts were 2, 3, 5, 8 and 12 dollars. What is the variance of the amounts? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 30 / 5 = 6. Distances: -4, -3, -1, 2, 6. Squared: 16, 9, 1, 4, 36. The sum is 66, and 66 / 5 = 13.2.

questions.skill: Compute a variance
questions.stem: In a survey, 3 students read 2 books, 4 students read 5 books and 3 students read 8 books. What is the variance of the number of books read by the 10 students? (The variance is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is (3 x 2 + 4 x 5 + 3 x 8) / 10 = 50 / 10 = 5. Squared distances: 9 for each of the three 2s, 0 for the 5s, 9 for each of the three 8s. The sum is 54, and 54 / 10 = 5.4.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: Four metal rods measure 16, 28, 32 and 44 centimeters. Find the standard deviation of their lengths, in centimeters. (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 120 / 4 = 30. Distances: -14, -2, 2, 14. Squared: 196, 4, 4, 196. The sum is 400, and 400 / 4 = 100. The square root of 100 is 10.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: A club's seven members are 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 years old. What is the standard deviation of their ages, in years? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 14. Distances: -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. Squared: 9, 4, 1, 0, 1, 4, 9. The sum is 28, and 28 / 7 = 4. The square root of 4 is 2.

questions.skill: Compute a standard deviation
questions.stem: The overnight low temperatures on four nights were -7, -1, 1 and 7 degrees. What is the standard deviation of these temperatures, in degrees? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean is 0. Squared distances: 49, 1, 1, 49. The sum is 100, and 100 / 4 = 25. The standard deviation is the square root of 25, which is 5.

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: A data set has a variance of 0.49. What is its standard deviation?
questions.solution: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. Since 0.7 x 0.7 = 0.49, the standard deviation is 0.7.

questions.skill: Relate variance and standard deviation
questions.stem: A data set has a standard deviation of 0.5. Which statement about its variance is true?
choices: It is 0.25, which is smaller than the standard deviation
It is 0.25, which is larger than the standard deviation
It is 1, which is larger than the standard deviation
It is 0.5, which equals the standard deviation
questions.answer: It is 0.25, which is smaller than the standard deviation
questions.solution: The variance is the square of the standard deviation: 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25. Squaring a number between 0 and 1 makes it smaller, so 0.25 is less than 0.5.

solve.answer: It is 0.25, which is smaller than the standard deviation

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: List P is 10, 20, 30. List Q is 100, 110, 120. List R is 5, 20, 35. Which statement about their standard deviations is true?
choices: Q is the greatest, since its values are the largest
All three are equal, since each has three values
P and Q are equal, and R is the greatest
R is the greatest and Q is the smallest
questions.answer: P and Q are equal, and R is the greatest
questions.solution: Q is P with 90 added to every value, so P and Q have the same spread. R's values are farther from its mean (15 from it, against 10), so R has the greatest standard deviation.

solve.answer: P and Q are equal, and R is the greatest
solve.work: P: deviations -10,0,10; Q: -10,0,10 (same); R: -15,0,15, larger. P = Q, R greatest.

questions.skill: Compare standard deviations of two lists
questions.stem: List X is 4, 6 and list Y is 2, 8. How many times as large as the standard deviation of X is the standard deviation of Y?
questions.solution: X has a mean of 5 and each value is 1 away, so its standard deviation is 1. Y has a mean of 5 and each value is 3 away, so its standard deviation is 3. The ratio is 3 / 1 = 3.

solve.work: X: mean 5, deviations +-1, SD 1. Y: mean 5, deviations +-3, SD 3. Ratio 3 (same under either definition).

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: A data set has a standard deviation of 2. Every value is multiplied by 3. What is the variance of the new data set?
questions.solution: The new standard deviation is 2 x 3 = 6, so the new variance is 6 x 6 = 36. (The variance is multiplied by 3 x 3 = 9: 4 x 9 = 36.)

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: A data set has a mean of 10 and a standard deviation of 3. Every value x is replaced by 2x + 5. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
questions.answer: Mean 25 and standard deviation 6
questions.solution: Multiplying by 2 doubles the mean and the standard deviation (20 and 6). Adding 5 then shifts the mean to 25 but leaves the standard deviation at 6.

solve.answer: Mean 25 and standard deviation 6
solve.work: Mean 2*10 + 5 = 25; SD 2*3 = 6 (adding 5 does not change spread).

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: Every value in a data set is replaced by its negative. The old mean was 12 and the old standard deviation was 4. What are the new mean and standard deviation?
questions.answer: Mean -12 and standard deviation 4
questions.solution: The mean changes sign with the values, giving -12. The distances from the mean stay the same, so the standard deviation stays 4; a standard deviation is never negative.

solve.answer: Mean -12 and standard deviation 4

questions.skill: Effect of changing every value on mean and spread
questions.stem: Daily temperatures in Celsius have a standard deviation of 5 degrees. A weather site converts every temperature to Fahrenheit with F = 1.8C + 32. What is the standard deviation of the Fahrenheit temperatures?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 1.8 multiplies the standard deviation by 1.8, and adding 32 does not change it. So 5 x 1.8 = 9.

solve.work: SD scales by 1.8; +32 has no effect: 1.8*5 = 9.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Four values are all 10, so their standard deviation is 0. A fifth value, 30, is added. What is the standard deviation of the five values? (The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which is the mean of the squared distances from the mean.)
questions.solution: The mean of 10, 10, 10, 10, 30 is 70 / 5 = 14. Squared distances: 16, 16, 16, 16, 256. The sum is 320, and 320 / 5 = 64. The square root of 64 is 8.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: A data set has an extreme outlier added to it. Which one of these four measures changes the least?
questions.answer: The IQR
questions.solution: The range, the standard deviation and the mean all depend on how large the extreme value is. The IQR depends only on the middle half of the ordered data, so it changes least.

solve.answer: The IQR
solve.work: Mean, SD and range are all pulled by an extreme value; IQR is resistant and changes least.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: Six house prices, in tens of thousands of dollars, have a mean of 18. The highest price, 58, is an outlier. What is the mean of the other five prices, in tens of thousands of dollars?
questions.solution: The six prices total 6 x 18 = 108. Without the outlier the total is 108 - 58 = 50. Dividing by 5 gives 10.

questions.skill: Effect of an outlier
questions.stem: The data 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 get a new value, 100. Which statement is true about the new data set?
choices: The median grows a lot while the range changes only a little
The range grows a lot while the median changes only a little
The range and the median both stay the same
The range and the median both grow by about the same amount
questions.answer: The range grows a lot while the median changes only a little
questions.solution: The range jumps from 4 to 95. The median moves only from 7 to 7.5, since it depends on the middle of the ordered list.

solve.answer: The range grows a lot while the median changes only a little

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: A researcher records the yearly incomes of 50 people. A few people earn far more than the rest, so the data are strongly skewed. Which pair of measures best summarizes them?
choices: The mean and the standard deviation
questions.answer: The median and the IQR
questions.solution: With skewed data and large outliers, the median and the IQR are resistant to the extreme incomes, so they describe the typical value and spread best.

solve.answer: The median and the IQR
solve.work: Skewed data: resistant median and IQR.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: For which data set is the IQR a better measure of spread than the standard deviation?
choices: Race times, where one runner stopped for 20 minutes
Heights of 30 students in a class, with no extreme values
Weights of identical boxes, which hardly vary
Quiz scores that are evenly spread around the mean
questions.answer: Race times, where one runner stopped for 20 minutes
questions.solution: The runner who stopped is an outlier that inflates the standard deviation. The IQR ignores it. The other sets have no extreme values.

solve.answer: Race times, where one runner stopped for 20 minutes
solve.work: Only the race times have an extreme value, where IQR is preferable.

questions.skill: Choose a measure of spread
questions.stem: A data set has a range of 80, an IQR of 6 and a standard deviation of 25, because of one extreme value. Which measure best describes how much the typical values vary?
questions.answer: The IQR of 6
questions.solution: The range and standard deviation are inflated by the extreme value. The IQR uses only the middle half of the data, so it reflects the typical variation.

solve.answer: The IQR of 6
solve.work: One extreme value inflates range and SD; IQR of 6 describes typical variation. The mean is not a spread measure.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: Mia scored 82 on a test with a mean of 70 and a standard deviation of 6. Leo scored 90 on a different test with a mean of 80 and a standard deviation of 10. Who did better compared with their own test takers?
choices: Leo, because his score of 90 is the higher of the two scores
Mia and Leo did equally well, since both scored above their means
Mia, who is 2 standard deviations above her mean while Leo is 1
Leo, because his test has the larger standard deviation
questions.answer: Mia, who is 2 standard deviations above her mean while Leo is 1
questions.solution: Mia is 12 / 6 = 2 standard deviations above her mean. Leo is 10 / 10 = 1 standard deviation above his. Mia did better relative to her group.

solve.answer: Mia, who is 2 standard deviations above her mean while Leo is 1
solve.work: Mia (82-70)/6 = 2; Leo (90-80)/10 = 1. Mia did better relatively.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: The scores on a test have a mean of 85 and a standard deviation of 7.5. What score is 2 standard deviations below the mean?
questions.solution: 2 standard deviations is 2 x 7.5 = 15 points. Below the mean: 85 - 15 = 70.

questions.skill: Interpret standard deviation in context
questions.stem: Weights of packages have a mean of 60 kilograms and a standard deviation of 12 kilograms. What is the smallest weight that is within 2 standard deviations of the mean, in kilograms?
questions.solution: 2 standard deviations is 2 x 12 = 24 kilograms. The smallest weight within that distance of the mean is 60 - 24 = 36.

questions.skill: Compare distributions by centre and spread
questions.stem: Baker P sold 12, 12, 20 and 20 loaves on four days. Baker Q sold 15, 15, 17 and 17 loaves. Which statement is true?
choices: Both have a mean of 16, and P has the greater standard deviation, 4 against 1
Both have a mean of 16, and Q has the greater standard deviation, 4 against 1
Q has the greater mean, and P has the greater standard deviation
P has the greater mean, but they have the same standard deviation
questions.answer: Both have a mean of 16, and P has the greater standard deviation, 4 against 1
questions.solution: Both sets total 64, so both means are 16. P's values are 4 from the mean (standard deviation 4). Q's are 1 from the mean (standard deviation 1).

solve.answer: Both have a mean of 16, and P has the greater standard deviation, 4 against 1
solve.work: P: mean 64/4 = 16, deviations +-4, SD 4. Q: mean 64/4 = 16, deviations +-1, SD 1.

questions.skill: Compare distributions by centre and spread
questions.stem: Hannah ran a mile in 12 minutes in a group with a mean of 9 minutes and a standard deviation of 1 minute. Eli ran in 14 minutes in a group with a mean of 11 minutes and a standard deviation of 3 minutes. How many more standard deviations above its group's mean is Hannah's time than Eli's?
questions.solution: Hannah is 3 minutes above her mean, which is 3 / 1 = 3 standard deviations. Eli is 3 minutes above his, which is 3 / 3 = 1 standard deviation. The difference is 3 - 1 = 2.

questions.skill: Compare distributions by centre and spread
questions.stem: Two lists both have a mean of 10. List A is 7, 9, 10, 11, 13 and list B is 4, 8, 10, 12, 16. The standard deviation of B is how many times the standard deviation of A?
questions.solution: List A: squared distances 9, 1, 0, 1, 9, so the variance is 20 / 5 = 4 and the standard deviation is 2. List B: squared distances 36, 4, 0, 4, 36, so the variance is 80 / 5 = 16 and the standard deviation is 4. The ratio is 4 / 2 = 2.

solve.work: A deviations -3,-1,0,1,3, squares sum 20. B deviations -6,-2,0,2,6 = 2x A's, squares sum 80. SD ratio sqrt(80/20) = 2.

questions.skill: Use technology output for spread
questions.stem: A calculator shows a mean of 52 and a standard deviation of 4.5 for a list of numbers. The same list is entered again with 3 added to every value. What will the calculator show?
questions.answer: Mean 55 and standard deviation 4.5
questions.solution: Adding 3 to every value moves the mean up by 3, to 55, and leaves the spread, so the standard deviation, at 4.5.

solve.answer: Mean 55 and standard deviation 4.5
solve.work: Adding 3 shifts mean to 55; SD unchanged 4.5.

questions.skill: Use technology output for spread
questions.stem: A spreadsheet reports a variance of 20.25 for a set of lengths in centimeters. What is the standard deviation of the lengths, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The standard deviation is the square root of the variance. Since 4.5 x 4.5 = 20.25, it is 4.5.

questions.skill: Compare spread without computing
questions.stem: Set A is 2, 10 and set B is 2, 6, 10. (The standard deviation is the square root of the mean of the squared distances from the mean: divide by the number of values.) Which statement about the two standard deviations is true?
choices: They are equal, since both sets have the same mean, which is 6
Set B's is greater, since set B has one more value than set A
They are equal, since both sets have the same range, which is 8
Set A's is greater, since set B's new value is at the mean
questions.answer: Set A's is greater, since set B's new value is at the mean
questions.solution: Both sets have a mean of 6. Set A: squared distances are 16 and 16, mean 16, standard deviation 4. Set B: squared distances are 16, 0 and 16, mean 32/3 (about 10.7), standard deviation about 3.3. The extra value 6 sits exactly at the mean, so it adds no spread but counts in the average, pulling the standard deviation down. Set A's is greater. Having the same mean or the same range does not make the standard deviations equal.

solve.answer: Set A's is greater, since set B's new value is at the mean
solve.work: A: mean 6, squared distances 16,16, variance 16, SD 4. B: mean 6, squared distances 16,0,16, variance 32/3 ~ 10.67, SD ~ 3.27. A's SD is greater; adding a value at the mean lowers the spread. Options 1 and 3 claim equal (false), option 2 claims B greater (false).

questions.skill: Compare the means of several populations
questions.stem: The mean test scores of students at three schools are 72 for School A, 78 for School B and 75 for School C. How many points higher is the greatest mean than the least mean?
questions.solution: The greatest mean is 78 (School B) and the least is 72 (School A). $78 - 72 = 6$ points.

questions.skill: Draw a conclusion supported by group means
questions.stem: A survey finds the mean number of minutes students exercise each day. Class 1 has a mean of 25, Class 2 has a mean of 40 and Class 3 has a mean of 32. Which statement is supported by these means?
choices: On average, Class 2 students exercise more than Class 1 students
Every student in Class 2 exercises more than every student in Class 1
On average, Class 3 students exercise more than Class 2 students
Class 1 students vary the most in how long they exercise
questions.answer: On average, Class 2 students exercise more than Class 1 students
questions.solution: Class 2's mean (40) is greater than Class 1's mean (25), so on average Class 2 students exercise more. Means say nothing about every individual student or about how much the students vary.

solve.answer: On average, Class 2 students exercise more than Class 1 students
solve.work: Class 2 mean 40 > Class 1 mean 25, so on average Class 2 exercises more. Means say nothing about variability or every individual.

questions.skill: Mean of three equal-sized groups
questions.stem: Three groups of 10 students each took a typing test. The mean scores, in words per minute, were 70 for Group A, 80 for Group B and 90 for Group C. What is the mean score of all 30 students?
questions.solution: The groups are the same size, so the overall mean is the mean of the three group means: $\frac{70+80+90}{3} = \frac{240}{3} = 80$.

questions.skill: Compare the means of several populations
questions.stem: Four clubs recorded how many books each member read last month. The means were 4 books for the Chess Club, 7 for the Art Club, 5 for the Drama Club and 3 for the Robotics Club. Which club had the greatest mean?
questions.answer: Art Club
questions.solution: Compare the four means: 4, 7, 5 and 3. The greatest is 7, which belongs to the Art Club.

solve.answer: Art Club
solve.work: Means: Chess 4, Art 7, Drama 5, Robotics 3. Greatest is 7, the Art Club.

questions.skill: Compare the means of several populations
questions.stem: The mean heights of sunflowers grown in Garden 1, Garden 2 and Garden 3 are $150$ cm, $162$ cm and $171$ cm. The mean height in Garden 3 is how many centimeters greater than the mean height in Garden 1?
questions.solution: Subtract the two means: $171 - 150 = 21$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Compare the means of several populations
questions.stem: Team A has 6 players who scored a mean of 12 points each. Team B has 6 players who scored a mean of 9 points each. How many more points did Team A's players score altogether than Team B's players?
questions.solution: A mean times the number of players gives the total. Team A scored $6 \times 12 = 72$ points and Team B scored $6 \times 9 = 54$ points. The difference is $72 - 54 = 18$ points.

solve.work: Team A total 6 x 12 = 72; Team B total 6 x 9 = 54; 72 - 54 = 18.

questions.skill: Combined mean of groups of different sizes
questions.stem: At a family reunion, one table has 3 adults with a mean age of 40 years and 2 children with a mean age of 10 years. What is the mean age of all 5 people, in years?
questions.solution: The adults' ages add to $3 \times 40 = 120$ and the children's ages add to $2 \times 10 = 20$. All five add to 140, so the mean is $140 \div 5 = 28$ years.

questions.skill: Combined mean of groups of different sizes
questions.stem: Class X has 10 students who own a mean of 3 pets each. Class Y has 10 students who own a mean of 5 pets each. How many pets do the 20 students own altogether?
questions.solution: Class X owns $10 \times 3 = 30$ pets and Class Y owns $10 \times 5 = 50$ pets. Together that is $30 + 50 = 80$ pets.

questions.skill: Combined mean of groups of different sizes
questions.stem: Group P has 20 students with a mean of 50 points. Group Q has 5 students with a mean of 90 points. What is the mean of all 25 students together?
questions.solution: Group P scored $20 \times 50 = 1000$ points and Group Q scored $5 \times 90 = 450$ points, so all 25 students scored 1450 points. The mean is $1450 \div 25 = 58$. The number 70 comes from averaging the two means as if the groups were the same size, which they are not.

questions.skill: Find a missing value or group mean from an overall mean
questions.stem: Four friends have a mean of 10 stickers each. Three of them have 8, 12 and 9 stickers. How many stickers does the fourth friend have?
questions.solution: Four friends with a mean of 10 have $4 \times 10 = 40$ stickers in all. The three known amounts add to $8 + 12 + 9 = 29$, so the fourth friend has $40 - 29 = 11$ stickers.

questions.skill: Find a missing value or group mean from an overall mean
questions.stem: Two classes of 20 students each took a quiz. Class A had a mean of 6 points. All 40 students together had a mean of 8 points. What was the mean of Class B, in points?
questions.solution: All 40 students scored $40 \times 8 = 320$ points. Class A scored $20 \times 6 = 120$ points. Class B scored $320 - 120 = 200$ points, so its mean is $200 \div 20 = 10$ points.

questions.skill: Find a missing value or group mean from an overall mean
questions.stem: A class of 20 students has a mean score of 80. A new student who scored 60 joins the class. Which statement is true about the new mean?
choices: It is less than 80 but more than 60.
questions.answer: It is less than 80 but more than 60.
questions.solution: The new score is below the old mean, so the mean goes down. But one score among 21 cannot pull the mean all the way down to 60. The new total is $20 \times 80 + 60 = 1660$, so the new mean is $1660 \div 21 \approx 79.05$. It would be 70 only if the two numbers 80 and 60 counted equally, but 20 students scored near 80.

solve.answer: It is less than 80 but more than 60.
solve.work: (20 x 80 + 60) / 21 = 1660 / 21 = about 79.05: less than 80, more than 60.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of several data sets
questions.stem: The ages of the seven players on a team are 11, 14, 12, 13, 15, 12 and 14. What is the median age, in years?
questions.solution: Put the ages in order: 11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 14, 15. The middle (fourth) of seven values is 13.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of several data sets
questions.stem: The median trip time on Route B is 25 minutes. What does that tell you about the trips on Route B?
choices: Half of the trips took 25 minutes or less.
The most common trip time was 25 minutes.
The shortest trip and the longest trip averaged 25 minutes.
questions.answer: Half of the trips took 25 minutes or less.
questions.solution: The median is the middle value when the times are put in order, so half of the values are at or below it and half are at or above it. It does not say every trip was 25 minutes, it is not the most common value (the mode), and it is not necessarily halfway between the shortest and longest.

solve.answer: Half of the trips took 25 minutes or less.
solve.work: The median splits the ordered trip times so that (at least) half are at or below 25 minutes. The others describe the mode, the midrange and a constant set.

questions.skill: Compare the medians of several data sets
questions.stem: Two groups of five students counted how many push-ups they could do. Group A: 12, 8, 15, 10, 9. Group B: 14, 20, 11, 13, 18. How many greater is the median of Group B than the median of Group A?
questions.solution: Group A in order: 8, 9, 10, 12, 15, so its median is 10. Group B in order: 11, 13, 14, 18, 20, so its median is 14. The difference is $14 - 10 = 4$.

solve.work: A ordered 8, 9, 10, 12, 15: median 10. B ordered 11, 13, 14, 18, 20: median 14. 14 - 10 = 4.

questions.skill: Compare the spread of several populations
questions.stem: The heights of five seventh graders are 142, 155, 150, 163 and 148 centimeters. What is the range of the heights, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least: $163 - 142 = 21$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Compare the spread of several populations
questions.stem: Three classes took the same quiz. The ranges of their scores were 4 points for Class A, 15 points for Class B and 9 points for Class C. Which class had scores that were closest together?
choices: All three, because they took the same quiz
questions.answer: Class A
questions.solution: A smaller range means the scores are closer together. Class A has the smallest range, 4 points.

solve.answer: Class A
solve.work: The smallest range means the scores are closest together: Class A, 4 points.

questions.skill: Compare the spread of several populations
questions.stem: Two bakeries counted the loaves sold on five days. Bakery A: 40, 55, 48, 52, 45. Bakery B: 30, 70, 50, 62, 38. How much greater is the range for Bakery B than the range for Bakery A?
questions.solution: Bakery A: $55 - 40 = 15$. Bakery B: $70 - 30 = 40$. The difference is $40 - 15 = 25$.

questions.skill: Compare percents when group sizes differ
questions.stem: In a class of 20 students, 15 walk to school. What percent of the class walks to school?
questions.solution: $15 \div 20 = 0.75$, which is 75 percent.

questions.skill: Compare percents when group sizes differ
questions.stem: Three classes were asked whether they have a pet. In Class A, 8 of 10 students said yes. In Class B, 15 of 20 said yes. In Class C, 30 of 50 said yes. Which class had the greatest percent of students who said yes?
choices: All three classes had the same percent
questions.answer: Class A
questions.solution: Class A: $8 \div 10 = 80\%$. Class B: $15 \div 20 = 75\%$. Class C: $30 \div 50 = 60\%$. Class C has the most "yes" answers, 30, but Class A has the greatest percent.

solve.answer: Class A

questions.skill: Compare percents when group sizes differ
questions.stem: In a survey of 200 people, 35 percent said they prefer tea to coffee. How many of the 200 people prefer tea?
questions.solution: 35 percent of 200 is $0.35 \times 200 = 70$ people.

questions.skill: Choose and justify a measure of center
questions.stem: Five quiz scores are 70, 72, 74, 76 and 78, so the mean and the median are both 74. A sixth score of 100 is added. Which statement is true about the new mean and median?
choices: The new median is greater than the new mean.
The new mean and the new median are both still 74.
The new mean and the new median are equal.
The new mean is greater than the new median.
questions.answer: The new mean is greater than the new median.
questions.solution: New mean: $(370 + 100) \div 6 \approx 78.3$. New median: the middle two of 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 100 are 74 and 76, so the median is 75. The very high score pulls the mean up more than the median.

solve.answer: The new mean is greater than the new median.
solve.work: New set 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 100: sum 470, mean about 78.3; median (74 + 76) / 2 = 75. Mean > median.

questions.skill: Choose and justify a measure of center
questions.stem: A list of values is 2, 4, 6, 8 and 20. How much greater is the mean of the list than its median?
questions.solution: The mean is $(2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 20) \div 5 = 40 \div 5 = 8$. The median is the middle value, 6. The difference is $8 - 6 = 2$.

questions.skill: Choose and justify a measure of center
questions.stem: Five workers' hourly pay rates, in dollars, are 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18. The greatest rate changes from 18 to 60. What is the median of the five new rates, in dollars?
questions.solution: The new rates in order are 10, 12, 14, 16, 60. The middle one is 14. The median did not change when the greatest value changed, because only the middle position matters.

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and recommend a plan from the data
questions.stem: A school compares three tutoring programs by the mean improvement in test score: Program A 6 points, Program B 9 points and Program C 4 points. The school can pay for only one. Which recommendation is best supported by these results?
choices: Choose Program A, because it was listed first.
Choose Program C, because it had the least improvement and so is the best value.
Choose Program B, because its students improved the most on average.
Choose no program, because the means are different.
questions.answer: Choose Program B, because its students improved the most on average.
questions.solution: The goal is improvement, and Program B has the greatest mean improvement, 9 points. Order of listing and a smaller improvement are not reasons to choose a program.

solve.answer: Choose Program B, because its students improved the most on average.
solve.work: Program B had the greatest mean improvement (9); the other reasons are irrelevant or illogical.

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and recommend a plan from the data
questions.stem: The mean trip time was 20 minutes on Route A and 14 minutes on Route C. Which reason for recommending Route C over Route A is supported by these data?
choices: It has more stops along the way.
It is listed after Route A.
Its mean trip time is 6 minutes shorter.
questions.answer: Its mean trip time is 6 minutes shorter.
questions.solution: Only the trip times are given: $20 - 14 = 6$ minutes shorter on Route C. Nothing in the data says anything about stops, the year it was built or the order of a list.

solve.answer: Its mean trip time is 6 minutes shorter.
solve.work: 20 - 14 = 6 minutes shorter on average; the other reasons are not in the data.

questions.skill: Draw conclusions and recommend a plan from the data
questions.stem: A school compares three study programs. The mean gain in test score was 8 points for Program A, 11 points for Program B and 5 points for Program C. If 40 students join the program with the greatest mean gain, how many points in total would the school expect them to gain altogether?
questions.solution: Program B has the greatest mean gain, 11 points. For 40 students the expected total is $40 \times 11 = 440$ points.

solve.work: Greatest mean gain is Program B, 11 points. 40 x 11 = 440.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and methods
questions.stem: A student wants to compare how many hours students at her school sleep. Which sample is most likely to represent all the students at the school?
choices: 10 students chosen at random from a list of every student
The first 10 students in the lunch line
The 10 members of the chess club
The 10 friends of the person doing the survey
questions.answer: 10 students chosen at random from a list of every student
questions.solution: A random sample from the whole school gives every student the same chance to be chosen. The other groups are chosen by something that may be linked to how much they sleep.

solve.answer: 10 students chosen at random from a list of every student
solve.work: A random sample from a list of every student is the representative one; the others are convenience or self-similar groups.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and methods
questions.stem: Which survey question is the fairest way to find out how many hours students sleep?
choices: Don't you agree that students should sleep 9 hours?
Students who sleep too little fail tests. How many hours do you sleep?
How many hours did you sleep last night?
Do you like to sleep a lot?
questions.answer: How many hours did you sleep last night?
questions.solution: A fair question does not push people toward an answer and asks for the number you want to know. The first question asks for hours directly. The others lead the answer or ask for something else.

solve.answer: How many hours did you sleep last night?
solve.work: The neutral, specific question is "How many hours did you sleep last night?"; the others are leading or vague.

questions.skill: Reflect on sampling and methods
questions.stem: Why is it better to survey 100 randomly chosen students than 5 randomly chosen students?
choices: A larger sample always gives the same results as a smaller sample.
A larger sample lets the surveyor choose which students to include.
A larger sample removes the need to ask a fair question.
A larger random sample is more likely to be close to the whole population.
questions.answer: A larger random sample is more likely to be close to the whole population.
questions.solution: With more randomly chosen students, one unusual student has less effect, so the results are more likely to be close to what the whole population would say. A bigger sample does not make the results identical, and it does not fix unfair questions or biased selection.

solve.answer: A larger random sample is more likely to be close to the whole population.
solve.work: A larger random sample tends to give results closer to the population.
